Śrī Kṛṣṇa said: Listen, O Rādhikā! Kṛṣṇanārāyaṇa is the Supreme Lord. He spoke to Devāyatanakā; I shall tell that to you as well. (1)
The installation of the tortoise-stone and the planting of the door-frames and so forth;
the installation of the lotus-stone and the entry of the *dhvaja-puruṣa* (the flag-man);
the installation of the bell and likewise the installation of the flag. (2)
The installation of a deity is considered to consist of seven auspicious days (puṇyāha).
Indeed, the worship of the site (vāstupūjā) must be performed there again and again.
I shall now tell you those fourteen rites of pacification (śāntikarma).
In the excavation of the foundation, in the offering of the tortoise, in the offering of the stone slab, in the ritual cord;
in the offering of the door, in the offering of the threshold, in the offering of the water-pot, and in the courtyard;
in the lotus-shaped mountain, in the Śukanāsa (the parrot-nose pinnacle), in the banner-man, and in the bell.
Indeed, there are various opinions regarding the offering of the banner upon the pitcher during the consecration ceremony.
At one time, however, the Supreme Brahman manifested his own form as an object of perception;
from that, a radiance arose, possessing the brilliance of ten million infinite suns.
Then the Lord, the master of yogis, who possesses the nature of dissolution, became manifest; at that time, a drop of sweat appeared from his forehead.
When that [drop] assumed the form of a personified being, it was terrifying.

Then, by the gods who had become Brahmās, he was placed face-down upon the earth. Of that Vāstupuruṣa, his feet, calves, and knees were then located in the southwest (Nairṛta), while his head was in the northeast (Īśāna).
Then his right elbow became Fire and his left became Wind;
thus, forty-five deities came to reside within his body.
Endowed with all these deities, he received worship and became the bestower of happiness.
A sixty-four-fold division, even if square, is worthy of worship.
An eighty-one-fold division, even if square, is worthy of worship. And one consisting of a hundred divisions, even if square, is worthy of worship. (12–13)
Eight deities reside in each of its eight pillars.
From one elephant, fifty elephants are prescribed.
Having fashioned thirty-two mandalas, one should worship them on all sides.
One should draw a site-plan (vāstu) consisting of sixty-four or one hundred squares using gems, gold, silver, coral, or even grains;
or, having made it with flour or unbroken rice, one should offer the sacrificial oblation (bali). || 15–16 ||

I shall show you the sixty-four-pada site-plan; listen to me. When the field has been made square and divided into eight parts, Brahmā is in the center occupying four parts, and likewise Aryaman is to his east.
In the south is Vaivasvata and the Maitra-gaṇa; likewise in the west.
In the north is Pṛthvīdhara, and similarly in the northeast when divided into two.
In the southeast, when divided into two, are Āpa and Āpavatsa.
Sāvitra and Savitṛ are likewise [placed] in the southwest (nairṛta) in two parts;
Indra and Jaya are also placed in the northwest (vāyu), divided into two.
After that, Rudra and Rājayakṣman are to be established.
Listen now to [the arrangement] all around in every direction according to the sequence of circumambulation:
in the northeast are Īśa and Diti; Parjanya is at the right ear;
Jayanta and Indra are on the shoulder; and then Sūrya, Satya, and Bhṛśa.
Ākāśa and Agni, then the two fires (Agni and Soma), Pūṣan, Vitatha, Gṛhakṣata, Yama, Gandharva, Bhṛṅga,
Mṛga, Pitṛs, and Āpa; then Nandika in the southwest (Nairṛta).
Sugrīva, Puṣpadanta, Varuṇa, and likewise the Asura,
as well as Śeṣa— these are established in the northwest wind;
thereafter, Nāga, Mukhya, Bhallāṭa, and Kubera [are situated].
Śaila and Aditi—thus the last one is situated on the left shoulder.
These indeed are to be worshipped in the sixty-four-fold division.
However, in the eighty-one-fold division, there are not two deities in each corner.
Each one indeed shall be a god; listen as I describe them to you:
Īśa, Parjanya, Jaya, Indra, Sūryaka, Satya, Bhṛśa, Ākāśa, Agni, Pūṣan, and Vitatha. (27–28)
Gṛhakṣata, Yama, Gandharva, Bhaga, Mṛga, Pitṛ, Nandī, Sugrīvaka, Pūṣan, Varuṇa,
Asura, Śeṣa, Pāpa, Roga, Nāga, Mukhya, and Bhallāṭaka.
Kubera, as well as Śaila, Aditi, and Diti;
Carakī is outside in the northeast,
Vidārikā outside in the southeast, Pūtanā outside in the southwest, and the wicked one is considered to be outside in the northwest.
In a square field divided into nine parts,
Brahmā occupies the center with nine squares, while Āryamā and the others occupy six squares each.
Those situated in the middle of the corners are proclaimed to occupy two squares.
The *abhitaḥ-pādika* should be known [to consist of] eighty-one squares; therein dwell the gods.
Now, O Rādhikā, listen as I describe the hundred-square site-plan (*vāstu*).
When the field has been made square and divided into ten parts, || 34 ||
All the outer corners should be empty, while the deities are situated on the right side.
In the center is Brahmā, occupying sixteen parts, and Aryaman and the others occupy six parts each.
Āpa and the others occupy two parts each; these auspicious ones should always be established and worshipped.
Īśa is at the head, and Parjanya is always situated in the right ear.
Jaya is on the shoulder; Indra, Sūrya, Satya, Bhṛśa, Ambara, and Sāvitra are on the arm; Savitṛ is in the hand; and Agni and the others, ending with Pitṛ, are in the foot.
Nandī and the others, as well as Roga and Kānta, reside in the left foot;
Maitra resides in the left thigh, and Vivasvat in the right thigh.
Indra is proclaimed to be in the secret region, and Jayanta in the portion of the anus.
Rudra and Rājayakṣman are likewise considered to be on the left hand.
Nāga, Mukhya, Bhallāṭa, Kubera, Śailaka, and Aditi—these are the serpents of the left arm; while Diti is on the left ear. (2.143.40)
Āpa is at the throat; Āpavatsa is in the heart; Aryaman is considered to be in the side.
Furthermore, Pṛthvīdhara is likewise considered to be in the right and left sides.
Carakī is in the northeast, and Cipicchā is considered to be in the east on the exterior.
Vidārikā is in the southeast, and likewise the guardians of the directions (dikpālas) are in the south.
Pūtanā is said to be in the southwest, and Skanda is in the west.
Pāpā and Rākṣasī are in the northwest, and likewise Kubera is in the north.
Thus, the deities within the body of the site (vāstu) are considered to bestow auspiciousness when worshipped.
Having constructed an altar two cubits in size to the north or the northeast of the temple,
one should spread there a silken cloth or a white garment.
There, having fashioned an unbroken svastika and then a yellow garment,
one should spread an eight-petaled lotus and perform the rite with unbroken grains right there. Then, having spread a red cloth over the yellow one, [one should proceed] there.
Having drawn the lines of the site with a golden needle or with barley-flour paste,
one should place a water-pitcher in the center at the Brahma-sthala.
O Gaṅgā, Yamunā, Virajā, Godāvarī, Sarasvatī!
O Narmadā, O Sindhu, O Kāverī, maintain your presence in these waters!
Viṣṇu shines at the front, Śiva in the middle, and Brahmā at the base;
the Mothers are all around, and within the belly are the oceans and tens of millions of sacred fords (tīrthas).
All the Vedas are in the form of leaves; the earth is in the form of jewels.
May the fruits [of my merit] rest upon this auspicious fruit (śrīphala). I establish you; be firm.
Oṃ, salutations to Śrī Siddhi; Oṃ, repeated salutations to Śrī Brahmā.
Oṃ, remain upon the beautiful and auspicious seat of Brahmā; salutations to the venerable Guru.
Oṃ, salutations to you, Vāsudeva, the architect of the universe; let there be salutation to you.
Indeed, the pure materials for worship have been sprinkled with water.
Everything becomes pure through the remembrance of Śrī Kṛṣṇa Nārāyaṇa.
Oṃ klīṃ, obeisance to Siddhi; come here, be firm in this place.
Oṃ, obeisance to Aryaman; come here, be steady in this place.
Oṃ, salutation to Vivasvat; come here and be firm.
Oṃ, salutation to Mitra; Oṃ, to Pṛthvīdhara, be firm.
Oṃ, salutation to Ṛddhi; come here and be firmly established in this place.
Obeisance to Āpa and Apavatsa; come hither, O you two who are steadfast! Obeisance to Sāvitrī and Savitṛ; Oṃ, come hither, O you two who are steadfast!
Obeisance to Indra and Jaya; Oṃ, come hither, O you two who are steadfast!
Oṃ, salutations to Rudra and Yakṣman; come hither, O you two steadfast ones!
Oṃ Hrīṃ Śrīṃ, salutations to Īśa; come here and be firm. Salutations to Parjanya, to Jaya, to Indra, and to Sūrya—Oṃ! 57–58.
Salutations intensely to Satya, and Om, salutations to Ākāśa!
Come here, arrive at this place, and remain firm in your own abode.
Om Klīṃ, salutations to Agni; come and remain firm in your place.
Oṃ, obeisance to Pūṣan Virocana; Oṃ, obeisance to Gṛhakṣata.
Oṃ, obeisance to Yama; obeisance to the Gandharva Bhṛṅga;
Oṃ, obeisance to Mṛga. Come, and remain firm in this place.
Oṃ klīṃ śrīṃ! Salutations to the ancestors; come hither and remain steadfast.
Salutations to Dauvārika and Sugrīva; be firm. Salutations to Puṣpadanta and Varuṇa; be firm.
Oṃ, be firm for the Asura Śeṣa and for Pāpa.
Oṃ klīṃ śrīṃ, obeisance to Roga; come here and be firm.
Oṃ, be firm for the chief Nāga and for Bhallāṭa. 63–64.
Salutation to Soma, to Śailā, and to Aditi; salutation to Diti, and to Sthirā.
Oṃ, salutation to Cipicchā; come here and remain firm.
Oṃ, salutation to Vidārī, to Jambhā, and to Pūtanā.
To Skanda, to the evil rakṣasī, and to Yama—here too, Oṃ, obeisance!
(66) Oṃ, obeisance to Carakī; come here and remain firm in this place.
Oṃ, repeated obeisance to you, the illustrious Great Lord of the Gaṇas. (67)
Salutations again and again to the chosen deities and to the family deities;
salutations again and again to the deities of the site and the dwelling, and to all others. Salutations again and again to the deities who preside over these primary and excellent rites.

In this eon, year, month, and day, for the sake of attaining my desired goal, I shall perform the worship of the deity Vāstudeva; salutations! Having bathed the god with the five nectars (pañcāmṛta) and water, [I shall apply] the sacred thread (brahmasūtra).
[One should offer] clothing, ornaments, a garland of flowers, incense, a lamp, and an offering of food; likewise, a bali-offering to the eight [directions], water for sipping (ācamana), betel leaf,
the waving of lights (nīrājana), circumambulation, prostrations like a staff, and so forth.
Then one should mutter the mantra: *oṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ kuru kuru svāhā*.
(72) One should also mutter twenty-one times: *nama oṃ vāstudevāya*. Then:
*oṃ pūrve hetakabhairavāya namaḥ*; and then in the south: (73)
Salutations to Ādivaitālabhairava in the west;
salutations to Kālabhairava in the north;
and salutations, Oṃ, to Ekapādabhairava in the zenith.
Salutation to Svacchandabhairava in the southeast;
salutation to Tripurāntakabhairava in the southwest;
and salutation to Agnijihvakabhairava in the northwest. 75–76.
"Obeisance to Vāyu-deva, and obeisance to Īśāna and Īśānaka;
obeisance to Oṃ in Pātāla, and obeisance, obeisance to Viṣṇu.
(77) Having offered the *arghya* and requested forgiveness, one should then bow to the Vāstu deity.
One should worship the guardians of the directions (dikpālas), the guardians of the fields (kṣetrapālas), Gaṇeśa, and likewise Caṇḍikā.
Then, one should perform all the rites beginning with the installation (pratiṣṭhā). [With the mantra:
"Oṃ Āṃ Īṃ Klīṃ, obeisance to Mahendra; remain firm in this place. (78–79)
"Accept, accept the offering together with the guardians of the field (kṣetrapālas) for Indra, svāhā!
Oṃ hrīṃ hroṃ hrāṃ, salutations to Vahni; remain firm in this place!
Accept, accept the offering together with the guardians of the field for Agni, svāhā!"
Oṃ krauṃ krauṃ krūṃ! Salutation to Kālamūrti; be firm here.
Accept, accept the offering (bali) together with the guardians of the field (kṣetrapālas); salutation, svāhā! Oṃ aiṃ kṣoṃ kṣīṃ! Salutation to Mṛtyu; be firm in this place.
Accept, accept the offering together with the guardians of the field (kṣetrapālas); homage, svāhā!
O Śrāṃ Śrīṃ Śrūṃ Vaṃ Viṃ, homage to Varuṇa; be firm!
Accept, accept the offering together with the guardians of the field; homage, svāhā!
Oṃ aiṃ, salutation to the Lord of the Universe; remain firm in this place!
Kṣetrapālas, accept, accept the offering (bali); salutation, svāhā!
Oṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ, salutation to Kubera; remain firm in this place! 84–85.

Oṃ klīṃ klīṃ klūṃ, salutations to Viśvaṃbhara; be firm! Oṃ klīṃ klīṃ klūṃ, salutations to Viśvaṃbhara; be firm! Oṃ klīṃ klīṃ klūṃ, salutations to Viśvaṃbhara; be firm! Together with the Kṣetrapālas, accept, accept this offering! Namaḥ svāhā! Together with the Kṣetrapālas, accept, accept this offering! Namaḥ svāhā! Together with the Kṣetrapālas, accept, accept this offering! Namaḥ svāhā!
Oṃ vrāṃ vrīṃ vrūṃ, obeisance to Brahmā; be firm in this place!
Kṣetrapālas, together with them, accept, accept the offering—obeisance, svāhā!
Oṃ śrāṃ śrīṃ, obeisance to the Lord of Śrī; be firm in this place! 87–88.
"O guardians of the field, together with them, accept, accept the offering! Homage! Svāhā!
Thus one should worship; thereafter, one should perform the rite of installation.
Indeed, performed in the months of Māgha or Phālguna, it bestows wealth, long life, and health.
An installation performed in the months of Jyeṣṭha or Vaiśākha causes the loss of wealth and sons.
When the sun is in its southern course (dakṣiṇāyana), one should likewise install the Vārāha, Mātṛkā, Bhairava,
Vāmana, Devī, and Nṛsiṃha [images].
In Śrāvaṇa, one should worship the Liṅga of Śaṅkara; in Āśvina, Jagadambikā;
in Mārgaśīrṣa, Hari Nārāyaṇa; and in Pauṣa, all the gods.
[This applies] on Saturdays, Sundays, Mondays, Wednesdays, Thursdays, and Fridays.
The height of the door should be divided into eight parts;
omitting the eighth part, one should proceed with three parts from the seven-part self-branch (ātmaśākhā).
The image should consist of two parts; this is the final determination regarding the *lamba*.
Having divided the door into nine parts, one should set aside one part.
Having divided eight parts into three, the image is considered to be two parts.
From one elephant-unit up to four elephant-units, there is an increase of six *aṅgulas* for each successive elephant-unit.
Then, up to ten elephants [in height], there is an increase of three *aṅgulas* for each elephant;
up to fifty elephants, there is an increase of one *aṅgula*.
Here, an increase of twenty parts from the measurement of the temple is considered excellent.
The *kolī* is said to be the largest according to the dimensions of the temple's purpose;
thus, O Devatāyana, you exist in such a manner.
My form is indeed the temple, and hear my meaningful form.
The palace is of divine form; its feet are known as the foundation stones (pādaśilā).
The base platform (jagatī) should be understood as the shanks, and the pillars are known as the knees.
The hip-bone (sakthi) should be understood as the decorative moldings (karmānikā), and the region below the pitcher (kumbha) is the penis (meḍhra).
The part corresponding to the anus is the water-spout (praṇāla), and the belly is considered the smoke-vent (ghūmmaṭa).
The navel is equivalent to the station of the deity, and the pedestal (pīṭhikā) is considered the heart.
This very living soul (jīva) is the image (pratimā), and the chest is the spire (śikhara).
The throat is the essence of purity (amalasāra), while the nose is the parrot-beak (śukanāsa). The eye is the lamp, the ear is the window, and the shoulder is the body-protector.
The head is the pitcher, the hair is the banners, and the elements are the constituent minerals.
In this regard, know that the flesh and fat are the plastering,
the earth and liquids are the bones, and the cloth is composed of powdered rags;
O King of Devotees, O temple of the Divine, understand your own body to be thus.

"Thus, O Rādhikā, Kṛṣṇanārāyaṇa spoke to him. Thus ends the one hundred and forty-third chapter, titled "The Description of the Installation of the Vāstu-Puruṣa, His Deities, and Others during the Pratiṣṭhā Festival," in the second section, the Tretā-Santāna, of the Śrī Lakṣmī-Nārāyaṇīya Saṃhitā. *Lakṣmī-Nārāyaṇa-Saṃhitā – Section 2 (The Lineage of the Tretā Yuga)*
Chapter 144 [Author:
Chapter 145 → Śrī Kṛṣṇa said:

Listen, O Rādhikā, to the procedure for the installation and other rites, as spoken by the primordial Lord Śrī Kṛṣṇa-Nārāyaṇa. Having bathed at dawn, the patron (yajamāna) shall offer [the materials] into the hand of the preceptor (ācārya).
Accompanied by women and married ladies carrying the materials for worship, [the officiant] should descend to the ground in front of the pavilion toward the eastern direction;
having washed his feet and sat down upon a seat, [he should proceed]. (2–3)
Having performed the ritual sipping of water (ācamana) and likewise the regulation of breath (prāṇāyāma), thereafter,
with his topknot tied and accompanied by his wife,
he should meditate upon Gaṇapati while facing either the east or the north, having proclaimed the place and the time.
For the sake of pleasing the Supreme Lord and for the successful accomplishment of the rite of installation (pratiṣṭhā),
one should perform the worship of Gaṇeśa, the selection of the preceptor (ācārya), and so forth;
one should also perform the washing of his feet and the worship of his feet.
Having worshipped him with moonlight, unbroken grains, flowers, and other offerings,
one should indeed bow down to that deity for the sake of accomplishing the rite in this beautiful temple,
for the sake of the successful consecration, and for the successful completion of the pavilion and other necessary works. (7)
"I choose you, O venerable devotee of Śrī Hari, to be my preceptor.
(8) The preceptor, who is learned in all matters, should say, "I am chosen.
Then the patron should tie the preceptor’s ritual bracelet. (9)
Having performed the worship of the preceptor, one should then invoke the Earth:
"Come, O Vasudhā, bestower of all auspiciousness; be firm here.

Then a beautiful wall made of bricks should be constructed;

Having fashioned it according to the form described previously, one should likewise construct a pavilion to its north.
Having prepared [the site] for the purpose of the ritual ablution, one should construct three altars (vedikās).

Having slept on the ground at night, practicing celibacy, and remaining highly sattvic,

For the sake of liberation from his transgression, he should then offer a "sin-cow" (pāpadhenu) as an act of expiation.

"May I possess the fitness for the work of building a temple for the gods on this very day"—thinking thus, for the sake of gaining merit and likewise for the removal of sins, one should offer the "sin-cow" to a Brahmin, saying: "I give [this] to you. (38–39)

Free from bonds, I shall offer the oblation to the deities; ordain that accordingly.

Saffron, sandalwood paste, musk, camphor, agallochum,

Grapes, plantains, and even fresh saffron and other such items;

seats, and a beautiful triple-threaded cord smeared with saffron.

There were ten banners made of excellent plantain-stalks, and their flagstaffs were made of bamboo;

[These were adorned with] diamonds, pearls, lapis lazuli, conch-shells, crystal, and topaz.
Indranīla and mahānīla gems, as well as the eight precious jewels; realgar, yellow orpiment, mica, and black antimony;
honey-stone, kāsīsa, gold-stone, and red ochre.

"Let this [sacrifice] indeed be complete, following the word of the Brāhmaṇas.

Thus ends the one hundred and forty-fifth chapter, titled "Description of the Installation of the Vessel, the Recitation of the Auspicious Day (*puṇyāhavācana*), the Invocation of the Mothers, the *Nāndī-śrāddha*, the Worship of the Seat, the Offering of Food, the Giving of the Fee (*dakṣiṇā*), the Dismissal, and so forth," in the second section, the Tretā-santāna, of the glorious *Lakṣmī-Nārāyaṇīya-Saṃhitā*.
Chapter 146 *Lakṣmī-Nārāyaṇa-Saṃhitā* – Section 2 (The Lineage of the Tretā Yuga)

Śrī Kṛṣṇa said:
O Rādhikā, listen to what follows after the Nāndī-śrāddha.
To his devotee, the Blessed One spoke regarding the selection of the preceptor and others as follows:
"Oṃ! Since this installation must be performed through ritual acts, I choose you, O Brahmin, as my preceptor with offerings of scents, unbroken rice, and other articles."
I am honored with flowers, betel, seals, and garments—Oṃ!
Having worshipped him, one should then perform the formal selection of the Brahmā priest. Oṃ! Regarding these rites that must be performed during this consecration ceremony...
I choose you for the office of the Brahman, observing the performed and the unperformed among the priests; O Brahman, I choose you for the station of the Brahman.
(4) With perfumes, flowers, unbroken rice, betel, ritual gestures, garments, and other offerings, [I declare]:

Having honored them with perfumes, unbroken rice grains, and other offerings,

The sacrificer should also appoint two reciters for each of the Vedas.
In this manner, there are twenty-five officiating priests (ṛtvij).
Alternatively, if one is unable to do so, one may instead appoint eight for the office of the Hotṛ priest,
four chanters (jāpaka), four gatekeepers, and the Guru.
Thus, indeed, there are seventeen officiating priests (ṛtvij).
Alternatively, there are four Hotṛs,
four reciters (jāpaka), four gatekeepers, and the preceptor (guru)— making thirteen.
Alternatively, the sacrificer should likewise choose both an Ācārya and a Brahmā;

A king, however, may choose as many as a hundred thousand, according to his strength.
Then one should worship the preceptor and others according to the prescribed rite, following the order of invitation.
One should indeed honor them with *madhuparka* and sweet milk-rice (*pāyasa*) and the like.
*Madhuparka* is of many kinds, consisting of sweet, sour, and other flavors, such as milk-rice and so forth.
Then the sacrificer, rising with palms joined in reverence, should entreat the Brahmins:

Oṃ bhūrbhuvaḥ svaḥ, O Pṛthivīdhara, come and remain!
And within the center of the site, I remember and invoke Brahmā:
"O you who are the form of Brahman, homage be to you; grant us the source of existence.
Oṃ bhūr bhuvaḥ svaḥ! O Brahmā, come here and remain here. (136–137)
In the outer northeast corner, I remember Carakī as well.
I invoke Carakī; I bow to her, the destroyer of bonds.
Oṃ bhūrbhuvaḥ svaḥ, O Carakī, come here and remain here!
In the southeast corner outside the fire-pit, I invoke Vidārikā.
O Vidārikā, destroyer of death, I bow to you, O Yoginī!
Oṃ bhūr bhuvaḥ svaḥ, Vidārikā, come here and remain! (2.146.140)
In the southwest corner, I invoke Pūtanā and I bow to her:
"O Pūtanā, destroyer of bonds, you who remove the misfortunes of Nirṛti!
Oṃ bhūr bhuvaḥ svaḥ, O Pūtanā, come here and stay here! (141)
In the north-eastern corner, I invoke and I bow to Pāpinī.
Oṃ bhūrbhuvaḥ svaḥ! O Pāpī, come here and stay here.
In the east, I bow to Skanda, I invoke him, and I remember him. 142–143.
O General, protect us from arrows; may the Destroyer of Evil grant us refuge.
Oṃ bhūr bhuvaḥ svaḥ! O Skanda, come here and remain here.
I bow to Aryaman in the south, I invoke him, and I remember him.
Oṃ bhūr bhuvaḥ svaḥ! O Aryaman, come hither and remain!
(145) In the west, I bow to Jṛmbhaka; I invoke him and I remember him.
Svāhā to him who neighs, snorts, lies down, and leaps! (146)
Hail to him who sleeps and who is awake; hail to him who yawns and who coos!
Oṃ bhūr bhuvaḥ svaḥ! O Jṛmbhaka, come hither and stay!
(147) In the north, I bow to Pilipiccha; I invoke him and meditate upon him.
To Pilippilākī and Piśāṅginī, svāhā! Let there be homage to you here.
Oṃ bhūḥ bhuvaḥ svaḥ! O Pilipiccha, come hither and stay! In the east, I remember Indra; I invoke him and I bow to him. 148–149.
Oṃ bhūr bhuvaḥ svaḥ! O Indra, come hither and stay here.
I remember Agni within the fire; I invoke him and I bow to him.
Oṃ bhūr bhuvaḥ svaḥ! O Agni, come hither and stay here.
In the south, I remember Yama, I invoke him, and I bow to him.
Oṃ bhūr bhuvaḥ svaḥ! O Yama, come hither and stay here.
In the southwest, I remember Nirṛti, I invoke him, and I praise him. (151–152)
Oṃ bhūr bhuvaḥ svaḥ! O Nirṛti, come here and stay here!
In the west, I remember Varuṇa; I invoke him and I bow to him.
(153) Oṃ bhūr bhuvaḥ svaḥ! O Varuṇa, come here and stay here!
I remember Vāyu in the northwest; I praise him and I invoke him.
Oṃ bhūrbhuvaḥ svaḥ! O Vāyu, come here and stay here.
I remember Kubera in the north; I invoke him and I praise him. 154–155.
Oṃ bhūrbhuvaḥ svaḥ, O Kubera, come here and stay here.
In the northeast, I invoke the god Īśāna and I bow to him.
Oṃ bhūrbhuvaḥ svaḥ, O Īśāna, come here and stay here.
In the middle between the northeast and the east, I indeed call to mind Brahmā.
I invoke him and bow to him; may the gods protect me on all sides.
O Bhūr Bhuvaḥ Svaḥ! O Brahmā, come here and remain here. (157–158)
Between Varuṇa and Nirṛti, I remember and praise Ananta;
I invoke Ananta, the Hari who provides protection against poison.
Oṃ bhūrbhuvaḥ svaḥ, O Ananta, come here and remain.

O Rādhikā, having thus invoked the deities of the Vāstu-pīṭha and bowed down to them, one should then perform the installation of the deity—including all its limbs and sub-limbs—during the sacrifice. Bṛhaspati established him; O Viśvedevas, be established! (2.146.160–161)
"Thus indeed did the divine Śrī Kṛṣṇa-Nārāyaṇa speak;
that very same *vāstu-dhyāna* has been proclaimed by me here for you.

Thus ends the one hundred and forty-sixth chapter, titled "The Description of the Selection of the Preceptor, Priests, and Others at the Consecration Festival, the Sprinkling of Materials, the Utterance of Auspicious Verses, the Worship of the Pavilion, and the Invocation of the Deities of the Vāstu-Pīṭha," in the second section, the Tretā-Santāna, of the *Śrī Lakṣmī-Nārāyaṇīya Saṃhitā*.

Śrī Kṛṣṇa said:
Listen, O Rādhikā; I shall tell you that which the all-pervading Anādi-Kṛṣṇa-Nārāyaṇa spoke concerning the abode of the gods. (1)

Since the worship of the deities of the site (vāstudeva) must be performed immediately after the consecration, a new copper pitcher, which constitutes the very limb of that [deity], should be installed with the mantra:
"Oṃ, smell the pitcher; may the Indus enter thee through the great [earth]."
"May the thousand-streamed, milk-abounding [waters] enter you; remain firm!
(3). Having thus established the pitcher, one should fill it with water:
"The pleasant abode of Varuṇa, the supporting water, is within you. (4)
"O you who are the seat of Truth, indeed, bestow the purifying water.
Having thus filled [the vessel] with water, one should wrap a cloth around the neck [of the vessel].
"You are the purifier of the garment, possessing a hundred streams and a thousand streams."
Having thus wrapped it with cloth, one should place the areca nut (*pūgīphala*) into the jar.
*Oṃ*. May you be fruitful and flowering; may you be fruitless and flowerless as well—such is your power. O areca nut, abide in this jar and become the bestower of fruits upon embodied beings.
Having thus offered a betel nut, one should present the five jewels:
gold, silver, diamond, ruby, and likewise pearl.
"The lord of the wandering mendicants, the sage Agni, has approached the oblations. (RV 10.8.6)
Thus, having given the jewels, one should cast gold into the jar:
"The offspring of Agni, which was formerly held upon his head by the God, that gold was carried away by Hari; I offer it into the jar. (2.147.10)
Having thus offered gold, one should place fragrance into the pitcher, saying:
"I offer you saffron, kesara, and sandalwood fragrance.
Having thus offered the fragrance, one should then present the medicinal herbs.
"Formerly, these [plants], overflowing with juices and dripping honey, were born upon the body of Hari.
I shall indeed cast even those seven hundred and seven *rudhanas* [into it].
Having thus offered all the medicinal herbs, one should present the seven types of earth.

One should offer [the earth] produced from an elephant, a horse, or a cow-pen, or that arising from an anthill or a crossroads, or obtained from a royal crossroads, or that grown at the root of a *tulasī* plant.
"O Earth, you who possess all forms, grant me happiness; O Vasudhā! [Thus one should pray.]
Having thus offered the seven types of earth, one should present *dūrvā* grass into the pitcher with the mantra:
"O *dūrvā*, growing from joint to joint, from stalk to stalk, may you spread for us by the hundreds and by the thousands. (16)
Having thus placed *dūrvā* grass in the jar, one should indeed offer the five types of sprouts [with the mantra]:
"O Aśvattha trees, you are our seat; on the Parṇa tree, your dwelling has been made.
Since you have indeed become sharers of the cows, do not harm this man. (17)
Oṃ, salutations!
At the mouth of the jar, I place fresh leaves indeed from the Aśvattha, the Vaṭa, the Cūta, the Udumbara, and the Plakṣa; may your kingdom flourish like a crop of grain.
Oṃ, may that which is pure, known as the purifier, sanctify [this] like the rays of the sun.
O Lord of the Purifier, I offer this purifying thread here into the jar.
Oṃ, salutations to you, the Purifier, born of *kuśa* grass, the Creator.
"I cast you into the jar; make that water pure.
Having spoken thus and placed the *pavitra* upon the jar, one should set down a new, beautiful golden vessel filled with unbroken rice grains (*akṣata*) and mixed with sugar and other ingredients.
"O full ladle, fly away; well-filled, fly back again!
Like two merchants trading goods, let us exchange food and strength, O Śatakratu!
(23). Having thus bowed to the vessel of rice, one should offer a bilva fruit.
Śrī, Lakṣmī, Ramā, Rādhā, Brahmavidyā, Satī, Rati, Suguṇā, Mañjulā, Haṃsā, Lalitā, Kambharā,
Satī, Santoṣā, Māṇikī, Durgā, Amṛtāmbā, and Śāradā— these [are her names]. (24–25)
"May they dwell here in this *śrīphala* (bilva fruit); may they be our enjoyers of prosperity.
Having thus placed the *śrīphala*, the officiant should bow to that bestower of fortune (*śrīda*).
"Oṃ! May the mind-impelled [sacrificial fire] partake of the clarified butter; may Bṛhaspati [partake of] the ritual."
"May this sacrifice be extended unimpaired; may it establish this one as well.
May all the gods rejoice here in this jar—Oṃ, be established!
(27). Having thus established the jar, one should then invoke Varuṇa.
Water indeed is rich in all flavors, purifying, and beneficial for sacrifice.
I approach that [water] with prayer, worshipping it; the sacrificer, with oblations, hopes for it from you.
O Varuṇa, being unangered, be mindful here; do not steal away the life of one who praises you extensively.
"Oṃ bhūr bhuvaḥ svaḥ! O Varuṇa, come here and remain here!
Having thus invoked Varuṇa, one should worship him with the sixteen articles.
All the oceans, rivers, sacred fords, and lakes [are invited].
And may they come for the sake of destroying the misfortunes of those who perform the sacrifice.
Kṛṣṇa is remembered as the mouth of the pitcher, Sadāśiva as its neck;
Brahmā himself is to be known as its base, and the Mothers are remembered as its belly.
The oceans are its cavities, and the earth is the form of the pitcher;
the Vedas together with their auxiliary limbs are indeed the constituent parts of the pitcher. I invoke the sacred waters: come hither and remain!
Born at the churning for the nectar of immortality, this jar was held in the hand of Viṣṇu.
You are the life-force of sacred fords, the dwelling place of gods and living beings, and you are the bestower of fruits.
The Ādityas, Vasus, Rudras, Viśvedevas, along with the Pitṛs, [reside within you].
"May the Aśvins abide in you; grant your presence for the sake of the sacrifice.
Having thus prayed to the pitcher, one should place upon it a golden image of Vāstu in the form of a lizard.
One should perform the rite of lifting the fire and cover [the site] with cloths and fabrics.
(37) Then, during the lifting of the fire, having proclaimed the place and time, one should meditate upon the Vāstu-purusha as a man lying supine with his head toward the northeast. (38)
And for the very purpose of avoiding defects such as those arising from threshing and so forth,
one should perform the rite of transferring the fire (*agnyuttāraṇa*) and the installation of the vital breaths (*prāṇapratiṣṭhā*).
Having placed the image in the vessel, one should cause a stream of milk to fall upon it.
Then one should pour a stream of water and recite the hymn again and again:
Oṃ! O Agni, we envelop you with the girdle of the ocean.
You who deliver all the gods, as the purifier, be auspicious unto us. (2.147.41)
Oṃ! With the caul of the snow, O Agni, we envelop you.
You who deliver us from all gods, as the purifier, be auspicious unto us. 42.
Oṃ! This is the gathering place of the waters, the dwelling of the ocean.
May those other weapons of yours, which take the form of obstacles, burn us.
O Purifier, who delivers all the gods, be auspicious unto us!
Homage to you, the burner and the flame; homage be to you, the radiance!
May those other weapons of yours, which take the form of obstacles, burn us;
O Purifier, who delivers all the gods, be auspicious toward us.
You are the giver of out-breath, the giver of in-breath, the giver of diffused breath, the giver of luster, and the giver of the most excellent [bliss].
"May those other missiles of theirs, which take the form of obstacles, burn us.
O Purifier, who delivers all the gods, be auspicious to us.
Having thus performed the rite of crossing over the fire, [one should perform it] with the five nectars.
Having bathed the Vāstupuruṣa, one should place him upon the water-jar (kalaśa).
One should meditate upon the form of Vāstu as it arose in the past from the Supreme Brahman.
Then, from the body of Śambhu, there was born a great and powerful son.
This one who obstructs the sacrifice has been defeated in battle by the gods.
Having been cast down face-down and bound on all sides by the hosts of deities,
his head is placed toward the northeast and the pair of his feet toward the southwest.
Having placed the knees upon the elbows and the two arms likewise,
then the knee toward the northwest and the southeast, and the joined palms at the heart;
having made the feet upward above that, all the gods became reddish-brown.
I invoke that Vāstuka, the source of all happiness.
Oṃ bhūr bhuvaḥ svaḥ! I invoke Vāstunara and offer salutations;
I honor you, so come, O you of great strength and prowess!
O son of Brahmā, whose body is the refuge of all the gods, homage be to you!
You are the sustainer of the entire universe; O Blessed One, come here!
O Blessed Vāstu, come here accompanied by all the gods.
Dwell here; perform what is auspicious; be present at this sacrifice.
Oṃ, Lord of the Dwelling, acknowledge us; be well-disposed toward us and free from disease.
Whatever we implore of you, grant that to us; be a source of blessing for our bipeds and our quadrupeds.
Having thus invoked [the deity] and worshipped with unbroken rice, flowers, sandalwood paste, garments, and ornaments, one should pray for protection: "Protect me from calamity and distress.
One should then offer the food offering, incense, lamps, the lustration ceremony (*nīrājana*), and so forth.
Then, having uttered "Svāhā," the physician should worship according to the prescribed rite:

"Oṃ, salutation to Śikhin, the Lord; likewise [offering] water for the feet (pādya), the arghya, water for sipping (ācamana), bathing water (snapana), clothing, perfume, and unbroken grains (akṣata). ||58-59||
I offer flowers, incense, lamps, food offerings, water, fruit, betel leaf, a bed, and a priestly fee; please accept them for my welfare.
*Parjanya*, salutations! Accept the water for washing the feet and other offerings, and grant me peace.

Salutation to Jayanta; accept the water for the feet and other offerings, and grant auspiciousness. (6.1) Oṃ, salutation to Indra; accept the water for the feet and other offerings, and grant auspiciousness.
Oṃ, salutation to Sūrya; accept the water for the feet and other offerings, and grant auspiciousness. (6.2)

Oṃ, salutation to Satya; accept the water for the feet and other offerings, and grant auspiciousness. Oṃ, salutation to Bhṛśa; accept the water for the feet and other offerings, and grant auspiciousness.
(63) Oṃ, salutation to Ākāśa, and salutation, salutation to Vāyu.
Oṃ, salutation to Pūṣan; Oṃ, salutation again and again to Vitatha.
Oṃ, salutation to Gṛhakṣata; Oṃ, salutation again and again to Yama.
Oṃ, salutation to Gandharva; Oṃ, salutation to Bhṛṅgarāja. 64–65.
Oṃ, salutation to Mṛga; Oṃ, and salutation again and again to the ancestors.
May they accept the water for the feet and other offerings, and grant welfare; salutation, salutation.
Oṃ, salutation to Nandin; Oṃ, and salutation again and again to Sugrīva.
Oṃ, salutation to Puṣpadanta and to Varuṇa; Oṃ, salutation!
(67) Salutation to Omasura and salutation to Śeṣa; salutation again and again!
Salutation to Pāpa and to Roga; Oṃ, salutation to Nāma and to Ahi. (68)
Oṃ, salutations to Mukhya and to Bhallāṭa; Oṃ, salutations and salutations again.
Oṃ, salutations to Soma, to the Nāgas, to Aditi, and to Diti.
Oṃ, salutations to the Maruts and salutations and salutations to Apavatsa.
May they accept the water for the feet and other offerings; may they grant well-being. Homage, homage! Oṃ, obeisance to Aryaman; Oṃ, obeisance to Sāvitra;
Oṃ, obeisance to Savitṛ, to Vivasvat, and to Indra—Oṃ, obeisance! (2.147.70–71)
Oṃ, salutation to Jayanta; Oṃ, salutation to Mitra; Oṃ, salutation!
Salutation to Rājayakṣman; Oṃ Oṃ, salutation, salutation to Rudra.
Oṃ, salutation to Pṛthivīdhara; Oṃ, salutation to Brahmā.
May they accept the water for the feet and other offerings, and may they grant well-being; salutations, salutations!
Om, salutation to Carakī; Om, and salutation to Vidārī;
Om, salutation to Pūtanā; and Om, salutation to Pāpā. 74.
Oṃ, salutation to Skanda; salutation to Aryaman; oṃ, salutation to Jṛmbhaka. Oṃ, salutation to Pilipiccha; oṃ, salutation to Indra.
Oṃ, salutation to Agni; oṃ, salutation to Yama; oṃ, salutation to Nirṛti. (75)
Oṃ, salutations to Varuṇa; Oṃ, salutations again and again to Vāyu.
Oṃ, salutations to Kubera; Oṃ, salutations to Īśāna.
Oṃ, salutations to Brahmā; Oṃ, salutations again and again to Ananta. (76–77)
May they accept the water for the feet and other offerings, and grant well-being; salutations, salutations! May you, Aṅgadeva and the others, accept the fragrance and the unbroken grains (akṣata).
[Accept] the flowers, incense, lamps, garments, and the food contained in each vessel.
I offer water, fruit, leaves, betel-leaf, sacrificial fees (dakṣiṇā), and so forth, as well as the waving of lights (ārātrika);
may they accept these and grant peace.
Then, one should again worship the Vāstupuruṣa in the same manner.
One should indeed perform the consecration of the vital breath (*prāṇapratiṣṭhā*), augmented by the seed-syllables and the *praṇava*.
Having made the heart one-pointed and meditated upon the Deity, one should recite:
*Oṃ āṃ hrīṃ krauṃ yaṃ raṃ laṃ vaṃ śaṃ ṣaṃ saṃ haṃ kṣaṃ haṃ saḥ so’ham.*
May the vital breaths (*prāṇas*) of this deity indeed abide here as vital breaths.
*Oṃ āṃ hrīṃ krauṃ yaṃ raṃ laṃ vaṃ śaṃ ṣaṃ saṃ haṃ kṣaṃ haṃ saḥ so'ham*.
May the life-force (*jīva*) of this deity indeed remain here as the life-force. *Oṃ*.
Oṃ āṃ hrīṃ krauṃ yaṃ raṃ laṃ vaṃ śaṃ ṣaṃ saṃ haṃ kṣaṃ haṃ saḥ so'ham.
Of this deity, [the constituents are] speech, mind, skin, eyes, ears,
as well as the tongue, nose, hands, feet, anus, genitals, and the internal organ.
And having come here, may they indeed dwell happily for a long time, svāhā!
(85) Oṃ! May the inspiration of the mind enjoy the clarified butter; may Bṛhaspati extend this sacrifice and establish this sacrifice as unimpaired. (86)
"May all the Viśvedevas rejoice here; Oṃ, be established!
Thus they worship with the sacrifice of establishment (pratiṣṭhā), and indeed [they honor] those who are established.
I perform the great pūjā for you, O Vāstu; grant me your grace."
Oṃ, salutations to the Vāstupuruṣa; I offer water for the feet (pādya).
(88) I give the water for honor (arghya), the water for sipping (ācamana), and the bath with the five nectars (pañcāmṛta).
I offer pure water and the sacrificial thread (yajñasūtra); salutations to you. (89)
I offer you clothing, fragrance, flowers, incense, a lamp, as well as a seat, food offerings, fruit, and betel; salutations to you!
I offer you a sacrificial fee, joined palms, and water for honor; salutations to you!
Oṃ! You are worthy of worship in the three worlds for the purpose of protecting the sacrifice.
Without your adoration, the excellent rites of the ritual do not succeed at all. O Blessed One, you who were born from the sweat on the forehead of Śambhu, you are without origin. 9.1–9.2.
"Accept this *arghya* offered by me; O Lord of the Dwelling (*vāstospati*), salutations to you!
Having thus presented the offering, one should then offer the *bali*.
*Oṃ*, salutations to Agni; here is an offering of milk-rice (*pāyasa*), [salutations].
Oṃ, obeisance to Parjanya; this milk-rice offering is mine.
(94) Oṃ, obeisance to Jayanta; this milk-rice offering is mine. Oṃ, obeisance to Indra; this milk-rice offering is mine. (95)
Oṃ, salutation to Sūrya; this milk-rice offering is for you. Oṃ, salutation to Satya; this milk-rice offering is for you.
(96) In this manner, [one should offer] repeatedly to each of the Vāstu deities individually.
"Oṃ, obeisance to Amukā; this milk-rice offering is mine.

(97) Thus one should present the bali-offering. Then, one should likewise offer to Carakī and the others, and also give bali-offerings of black-gram porridge to the guardians of the directions, as follows: (98)

Oṃ, salutation to Carakī; this offering of black-gram porridge is mine. Oṃ, salutation to Vidārī; this offering of black-gram porridge is mine. Salutation to Pūtanā; this offering of black-gram porridge is mine. (99)
Oṃ, salutation to Pāpā; this offering of black-gram and boiled rice is mine. Oṃ, salutation to Skanda; this offering of black-gram and boiled rice is mine.
One should also present [offerings] to Aryaman, to Jṛmbhaka, and to Pilipiccha. 2.147.101.

Salutation to Indra, Agni, Yama, Nirṛti, Varuṇa, and Vāyu. Salutation to Kubera, Īśa, Ajā, and Ananta; may this offering of black gram and boiled rice be accepted. (102) Then, one should indeed offer the bali-oblation to Vāstupuruṣa with the following mantra:
O Vāstu, accept this variously prepared offering of many fragrant cooked foods, including milk-rice and other delicacies; destroy the affliction of hunger.
Oṃ, salutations! This is an offering to the Vāstupuruṣa; may it be accepted.
May those gods who subsist on milk-rice accept this milk-rice;
may those gods who consume food accept this auspicious food and honey;
and may those gods who consume flavors accept these many flavors.
O gods who consume *kṛśara*, may you accept this offering of *kṛśara* rice. O gods who eat black gram (*māṣa*), may you accept this oblation made of black gram.
O gods who subsist on nectar (*amṛta*), may you accept that very nectar.
May those gods who subsist on flour-meal accept this flour-meal;
may those gods who consume fruits accept these fruits;
and may those gods who eat grains and those deities who feed upon mustard seeds [accept their respective portions].
O gods, may you accept this desired offering; let that which is appropriate for those who eat the sacrificial oblation—be it even just vegetables—be offered by me and accepted as my own.
Whatever is deficient in mantra, deficient in ritual action, or devoid of devotion and faith, [may it be complete through your grace].
O Lord, let that which has been offered by me be made complete.
Salutations to you, O Lord of the Vāstu-deities; be the remover of all obstacles.
Grant peace, bestow happiness, and grant me all my desires.
Oṃ, I offer this coconut to the venerable Vāstupuruṣa.
(1.12) And here I offer gold; I bow down to you, grant me happiness!
Śrīṃ! [I offer] Lakṣmī, Ramā, Rādhā, Brahmavidyā, and Padmajā. (1.13)
One should worship these— Suguṇā, Mañjulā, Padmā, Lalitā, Kaṃbharā, Satī, Santoṣā, Māṇikī, Durgā, Amṛtāmbā, and Śāradā—
with sāttvika offerings such as milk-porridge (pāyasa) and other pleasing substances, and thus satisfy them.
Then one should indeed encircle the pavilion on all sides with three cords,
making it resound with the *pavamāna* hymn which destroys evil spirits:
*Oṃ pavamānaḥ suvarjanaḥ pavitreṇa vicarṣaṇiḥ.*
May that which is the purifier purify me; may the divine beings purify me.
May the sages purify me with their wisdom; may all living beings purify me. O Jātavedas, with your purifying power, purify me by means of the filter.
O Agni, shining like a god with your brilliance, follow after our intentions with your wisdom.
O Agni, that filter of yours which is spread within your flame—with that sacred word (*brahman*), we purify ourselves. O divine Savitar, [we purify ourselves] by both means.
With the purifier and with the Soma-pressing, we cleanse this sacred prayer (brahman).
The purifying goddess belonging to all the gods has arrived, she whose forms have smooth backs.
Rejoicing with her in our common feasts, may we be masters of riches. (2.147.120)
May Vaiśvānara purify me with his rays; may Vāta, the swift and bliss-bestowing, purify me with his breath;
may Heaven and Earth, the observers of Truth and worthy of sacrifice, purify me with their milk and waters.
O Savitṛ, with your great, triple, and most excellent [purifications]—O God...
O Agni, purify me with thoughts and with skill—
that by which the gods purified themselves, that by which the waters [purified] the celestial *kaśa*—
with that divine prayer (*brahman*) we purify this prayer. 122.
Oṃ! I dig up this Valaga, the slayer of Rakṣasas, the slayer of Valagas, belonging to Viṣṇu—
this Valaga which my enemy and which my kinsman [have buried].
Whichever [person], whether equal to me or not equal to me, has buried this great *valaga*, I dig it up. Whichever [person],
whether equal to me or not equal to me, has buried this great *valaga*, I dig it up.
That which my kinsman or my non-kinsman has buried—
this great *valaga* (burial charm), I dig up.
That which my co-born or my non-co-born [has buried].
I have dug it out; having cut it up, I scatter it.
Oṃ! Display your power like a net; go forth upon the earth like a king with his retinue and his elephant. 125.
Pierce the swift-moving net of the one who rushes forward with arrows; strike down the Rākṣasas with your most scorching weapons.
May the divine beings purify my thoughts and intentions with their mind.
"O Jātavedas, [protect] all beings and me as well.
O Rādhikā! Having thus encircled the pavilion with three threads, one should then enter the pavilion and, having approached, take one's seat there.
Thus did Nārāyaṇa Kṛṣṇa speak, the refuge of the gods.
That very same thing has been told by me to you, even though not in great detail.

Thus ends the one hundred and forty-seventh chapter, titled "The Narration of the Installation of the Vessel, the Installation of Vāstu, the Worship, the Worship of the Vāstu Deities, the Offering of Food, the Bali-offering, the Encircling of the Pavilion with the Triple Thread, and the Mantras," in the second section, the Tretā-santāna, of the glorious *Lakṣmī-Nārāyaṇīya-Saṃhitā*.

Śrī Kṛṣṇa said:
Listen, O Rādhikā; thereafter, the primordial Kṛṣṇa-Nārāyaṇa spoke to Devāyatanakā. I shall tell those five things to you as well. (1)
Then, having invoked them according to the ritual procedure with the sixteen articles, one should worship the Yoginīs and Kṣetrapālas on the Vāyavya seat:
"Oṃ, I invoke the divine Yoginī; I establish her."
Oṃ, I bow to the divine Yoginī who protects the sacred field. (3) Oṃ, I invoke the Great Yoginī and I establish her here;
I worship her with perfumes and other offerings—to her, salutations again and again! (4)
Oṃ, I invoke the Siddhayoginī and I establish her;
I worship her with perfumes and other offerings—homage, homage to her!
Oṃ, I invoke the illustrious Gaṇeśvarī and I establish her.
I worship her with perfumes and other offerings; salutations, salutations to her! (6) Oṃ! I invoke, establish, and worship you—Pretākṣī, Ḍākinī, Kālī, and Kālarātrikā; salutations to you! (7)
I invoke, I establish, and I worship Niśācarī, Hūṃkārī, Siddhi, and Vetālinī; homage to you!
Oṃ Hrīṃkārī, Bhūtaḍāmarī, and likewise Oṃ Ūrdhvakeśī.
I invoke you, I establish you, and I worship you; homage to you!
(9) And Virūpākṣī, Śuṣkāṅgī, and Narabhojanā—Oṃ, likewise!
I invoke you, I establish you, and I worship you; homage to you! (2.148.10)
Oṃ, I invoke, establish, and worship Kaṅkārī, Vīrabhadrā, Dhūmrākṣī, and Oṃ Kalipriyā; salutations to you all!
[I invoke] Rākṣasī, Ghorarākṣasī, Virūpākṣī, and Bhayaṃkarī.
I invoke you, I establish you, and I worship you; homage to you! (12) Viśālākṣī, Kāmarī, Caṇḍī, and likewise Vārāhinī—I invoke you, I establish you, and I worship you; homage to you! (13)
I invoke, establish, and worship you—Muṇḍadhātrī, Bhairavī, Cakriṇī, Krodhā, and Durmukhī; salutations to you!
Likewise, [I invoke] Pretavāhanā, Kuraṅgī, Pralambauṣṭhī, and Mālinī.
I invoke you, I establish you, and I worship you; homage to you!
(15) I invoke Mantrayoginī, Kālāgnī, Mohinī, and likewise Vakrikā; I invoke you, I establish you, and I worship you; homage to you! (16)
I invoke, establish, and worship you—Kuṇḍalinī, Bālakī, Kaumārī, and Yamadūtī; salutations to you!
Oṃ, Karālī, Kauśikī, Yakṣiṇī, and likewise Bhakṣiṇī.
I invoke you, I establish you, and I worship you; homage to you! (18) I invoke Kumārikā, Yantravāhā, Viśālākṣī, and Kāmukī; I invoke you, I establish you, and I worship you; homage to you! (19)
Oṃ! Vādhrī, Rākṣasī, Pretabhakṣiṇī, and likewise Dhūrjaṭī—I invoke you, I establish you, and I worship you; salutations to you!
Oṃ! And Vikaṭā, Ghorā, Kapālī, and likewise Vimalā.
I invoke you, I establish you, and I worship you; homage to you!
(21) Oṃ, I invoke the garland of all accomplishments, and homage to you both!
I establish it and I worship it; may all [the goddesses] be granters of success. (22)

By this worship with the sixteen services (*ṣoḍaśopacāra*) and so forth, may the hosts of Yoginīs here be pleased; I offer this oblation of milk-rice (*pāyasa*). (23) Then, one should thoroughly worship the Kṣetrapāla and the deities of the sacred seats (*pīṭha*).
Om, I invoke the Ageless One and I establish him; homage to you!
I worship you and offer the sacrificial oblation; homage to you, the Ageless One! I invoke Indra’s Thief and I establish him; homage to you! 24–25.
I invoke, establish, and worship you—the pervasive one, the form of Indra, Ukṣṇa, Kūṣmāṇḍa, and Varuṇaka; homage to you!
[And] Vāmuka, Vimukta, Līlālopa, and Śaptaka.
I summon you, I establish you, and I worship you; homage to you!
(27) And Airāvata, Ekadaṃṣṭra, Oṣadhighna, and Bandhana—I summon you, I establish you, and I worship you; homage to you! (28)
I invoke, establish, and worship you—the divine-maker, the woolen blanket, the Gavaya, and the agitating one; salutations to you!
Likewise, [I invoke] Kāla, Baladhara, Aṇḍa, and Candravāraṇaka.

I invoke you, I establish you, and I worship you; homage to you! (2.148.30) I invoke Phaṭāṭopa, Jaṭila, Ṛtu, and likewise Ghaṇṭeśvara; I invoke you, I establish you, and I worship you; homage to you! (31)
I invoke, establish, and worship Vikaṭa, Cāṇima, Guṇabandha, and likewise Ḍāmara; homage to you!
Ṭhaṃṭhaphaṇa, Sthavila, Dantura, and likewise Dhanada.
I summon you, I establish you, and I worship you; homage to you! (33) I summon Nāgakarṇa, Photkara, Mahādala, and Cīraka;
I summon you, I establish you, and I worship you; homage to you! (34)
Oṃ, I invoke, I establish, and I worship you—the Lion, the Deer, the Yakṣa, and also the Cloud-Rider; homage to you!
Oṃ, [I invoke] Tīkṣṇauṣṭha, Anala, Sukratu, Yudhāpa, and Vakraka.
I invoke you, I establish you, and I worship you; homage to you! (36) Oṃ, I invoke Vāta and Yāpana, and I establish them;
I worship them, I offer the sacrificial oblation, and I bow down to them. (37)
"O fifty guardians of the fields, come here and remain here! [I offer] a seat, as well as water for the feet, the arghya offering, and water for sipping;
[furthermore,] bathing with the five nectars (pañcāmṛta), consecration, and garments."
Ornaments, sandalwood paste and other fragrances, unbroken grains of rice, saffron and the like, flower garlands, collyrium, incense, lamps,
food offerings, meals, drinking water, fruits, betel leaves and so forth. (2.148.39–40)
I offer the *nīrājana* and other rites; may they be my protectors.
Oṃ hrāṃ hrīṃ hruṃ svāhā! One should present an abundant offering (*bali*) to Baṭuka.
Indeed, all the *yoginīs* and *kṣetrapālas* who dwell there—
Therefore, having assembled here, may you accept my offering of nectar (amṛta).
Satisfied by this gift of oblation, may you grant me my desire;
may you perform the rites of the sacrifice and destroy all defects in my ritual.
Having thus given [the offerings] and made requests, one should prostrate to all the deities.
Then, one should perform the worship of the glorious pavilion (*maṇḍapa*) with the sixteen articles.
The patron (*yajamāna*), having been bathed by the officiating priests (*ṛtvij*) and the preceptor (*guru*), [should proceed].

Clad in white garments and white garlands, anointed with white perfumes and unguents, and accompanied by his wife, sons, and grandsons, he [the sacrificer] stands with the preceptor and the officiating priests;
while the sound of musical instruments resounds, the preceptor holds a full water-pot in his hand. (45–46)
Meditating upon the principal deity and intent on the visualization of the pavilion, the wise practitioner, while listening to the resonance of the Vedas, should worship the pavilion:
"Oṃ! May we hear with our ears what is auspicious, O Gods; may we see with our eyes what is auspicious, O Worshipful Ones."
With steady limbs and bodies, may we, offering praise, attain that life bestowed by the gods.

(48) Having sipped water, restrained the vital breaths, and proclaimed the place and time, one should perform the auspicious worship as a limb of the sacrifice for the installation of the principal deity. (49)
I perform the invocation, the installation, and the salutation of Gaṇeśa, the deity of the pavilion. Om! I invoke and install the illustrious Lord Gaṇeśvara.
I worship and prostrate with sixteen articles.

(51) Having thus worshipped Gaṇeśa and likewise offered the sacrificial food (naivedya), the sacrificer should then perform the worship of the pillars, starting from the northeast (īśāna) in due order. (52)
Om! In the northeast, I invoke the form of Brahmā, the Creator;
I establish him, the Grandfather, who holds a book, a rosary, a trident, and a water-pot, who is joined by his deities, and who is seated upon a swan. 53.
"Come, O Brahmā, creator of the universe, you who first dwelt within the pillar!
Om! Brahmā, the wise one, revealed from the front, from the boundless, the radiant light."
The foundations of his feet are the highest reaches; he has disclosed the womb of both the existent and the non-existent.
Om Om! Bhūr Bhuvaḥ Svaḥ! O Brahman, come here and remain!
Oṃ, salutation! I offer sixteen types of ritual services (upacāras) to you, O Brahmā.
Now, in the auspicious pillar in the southeast, I invoke Viṣṇu, the Lord of Ramā, who possesses four arms holding the conch, discus, mace, and lotus.
Seated upon Garuḍa, served by the hosts of Kamalā, Śrī, and Lakṣmī—come, O Blessed Viṣṇu, you who dwell in the second pillar!
I establish you as my Lord, I worship you, and I bow to you. 58.
Oṃ oṃ bhūr bhuvaḥ svaḥ, O Viṣṇu, come here and remain here.
(59) Oṃ, salutations to Viṣṇu; I offer you the sixteen types of service.
Oṃ, Viṣṇu strode across this universe; he established his foot in three places. (2.148.60)
"Salutation, salutation to you, Viṣṇu, whose foot is hidden in the dust!
Now, I invoke Śiva at the pillar in the southwest:
the one seated upon a bull, moon-crested, bearing the trident, and garlanded with severed heads. (6.1)
Attended by the host of Umā’s attendants, with a serpent as his sacred thread—O Blessed Śambhu, you who dwell in the third pillar, come!
I establish you, O Hara; I worship you and I bow to you.
Oṃ bhūrbhuvaḥ svaḥ! O Śambhu, come here and remain here.
Salutation! Oṃ, I offer the sixteen services (ṣoḍaśopacāra) to you, O Śambhu.
Oṃ, salutation to you, O Rudra, for your wrath and also for your arrow; salutation!
Salutations to you with both arms; Oṃ, salutations, salutations to you, Śambhu.
(65) Now, I invoke Indra at the pillar in the north-west corner—the thousand-eyed one, mounted upon an elephant, the wielder of the thunderbolt, and the lord of Śacī. (66)
Come, O Blessed Indra, dweller in the fourth pillar!
I establish you, Mahendra; I worship you and I bow to you.
Om bhūr bhuvaḥ svaḥ! O Indra, come here and stay.
Obeisance to Indra! Oṃ, I offer you the sixteen modes of worship.
Oṃ, I invoke Indra, the protector, Indra, the savior; at every call, I invoke the hero Indra, who is easily invoked.
I invoke Śakra, Indra, who is invoked by many. May the bounteous Indra bestow well-being upon us.

Oṃ, salutations to Indra; thereafter, I perform the worship of the twelve pillars on the outer part of the pavilion, starting from the northeast (Īśāna) in sequence. Now, in the northeast, I invoke and establish the Sun.
I worship here the one who is mounted upon a chariot drawn by seven horses, whose body is red, who possesses fierce brilliance,
who holds a lotus, who is situated upon the fifth pillar,
who is the very form of the eye of the three worlds, and who is resplendent with earrings and other ornaments. (71–72)
Oṃ. Moving through the dark expanse, establishing both the immortal and the mortal, the divine Savitṛ comes upon his golden chariot, beholding all worlds.
Oṃ bhūr bhuvaḥ svaḥ! O Sūrya, come here and remain here.
Accept this worship arising from the sixteen categories; homage be to you!
(74) Now, in the pillar between the northeast and the east, I invoke and establish Gaṇeśa, the elephant-faced remover of obstacles. (75)
I bow to Vināyaka, the bestower of success and wisdom. Come, O Lord of the Gaṇas, and remain upon the sixth pillar.
Oṃ, we invoke you, the Lord of the Gaṇas, among the hosts.

Oṃ, we invoke you, the beloved lord of the beloved. Oṃ, we invoke you, the lord of treasures. O Vasu, my own, I am the one who brings forth the offspring; may you bring forth the offspring within me. 77.
Oṃ bhūr bhuvaḥ svaḥ! O Gaṇapati, come here and stay!
Accept this worship consisting of sixteen articles; salutations to you!
(78) Now, on the pillar in the intermediate space between the east and the southeast, [one should invoke] Yama, the lord of Yama.
I invoke and establish [you], the one who strikes fear into all living beings;
I bow to the fierce-formed one of black complexion,
who holds a staff, whose vehicle is a buffalo, the witness of actions, and the embodiment of Dharma.
Come, O Dharmarāja, enter the seventh pillar:
*Oṃ, for Yama thee, for Makha thee, for the heat of the Sun thee!* (8.1).
May the god Savitṛ, the impeller, protect thee from the touch of the earth at night.
You are the flame, you are the radiance, you are the heat; you are the embodiment of Brahman.
Oṃ Bhūr Bhuvaḥ Svaḥ! O Yama, come here and stay!
Accept this worship consisting of sixteen articles; salutations to you.
Now, in the pillar at the southeast corner,
I invoke and establish the auspicious Śeṣa, the dweller of the netherworld, who possesses a thousand heads and is adorned with the jewels of his hoods upon a svastika-lined pedestal. (84)
I bow down to the god who is the seat of Nārāyaṇa and who is endowed with poison. (85) Come, O King Śeṣa, and enter into the eighth pillar.
Om, obeisance to the serpents, whoever they may be, that dwell upon the earth. (86)
To those who are in the intermediate space and those who are in heaven—to all those serpents, salutations, salutations!
Oṃ bhūr bhuvaḥ svaḥ! O Śeṣa, come here and remain here!
Accept this worship consisting of sixteen articles; salutations to you!

Then, in the pillar situated between Agni and Dakṣa, I invoke and establish the six-faced Skanda; indeed, I bow to Kārttikeya, the son of Śiva, who knows the Brahman of all principles and is seated upon a peacock. ||88-89||
Come, O you who are born of the reeds; enter the ninth pillar!
O Lord of the divine army, son of Ganga, son of Agni, Master!
Om! When you first cried out at birth, rising from the ocean or from the primordial waters (purīṣa).
The wings of a hawk and the forelegs of a deer—O steed, your great birth is worthy of praise.
Om Bhūr Bhuvaḥ Svaḥ! O Skanda, come here and stay;
accept this worship consisting of sixteen articles, salutations unto you.
In the pillar situated between the south and the southwest, I invoke, establish, and ever bow to Vāyu, the vital breath of embodied beings,
who is mounted upon a black deer, the support of all, and whose weapon is a banner.
(93) I invoke, establish, and ever bow to the Sadāgati.
Come here, O Vāyu-deva; enter into the tenth pillar.

Oṃ! O Vāyu, with those thousand chariots of yours, come hither, accompanied by your team of horses, for the drinking of Soma—[you who are] the vital breath, [bestowing] the boundless within ourselves.
Oṃ bhūr bhuvaḥ svaḥ! O Vāyu, come here and stay here!
Accept this worship consisting of sixteen articles; salutations to you!
[One should place] Soma, the lord of the night, upon the pillar in the southwest corner.

I invoke, establish, and bow down to the cool-rayed Śaśin, who resides upon the head of Rudra, who is white, and who is the son of Kṣīroda. O Lord Soma, come here and enter the eleventh pillar. || 97–98 ||
Oṃ, may you swell; let virility come to you from all sides, O Soma.
Be present at the gathering of strength, as the showerer of nectar and the nourisher.
(99) Oṃ bhūr bhuvaḥ svaḥ! O Lord Soma, come here and remain here.
Accept this worship arising from the sixteen topics; homage to you!
(2.148.100) In the pillar situated between Nirṛti and Varuṇa, there is the god Varuṇa, mounted upon a crocodile chariot, holding a noose in his hand, and blazing with splendor. (101)
I invoke, I establish, I bow down to Varuṇa, the Lord of Waters.
O Varuṇeśa, come here and enter the twelfth pillar!
(102) Om! Hear this my invocation, O Varuṇa, and be gracious to me today.
Desiring your protection, I, the dispeller of thirst and the creator of the *vipāś* [liberation from bonds], call upon you.
Oṃ Bhūrbhuvaḥ Svaḥ! Varuṇa, come here and remain;
accept this worship consisting of sixteen articles; salutations to you. 103–104.

In the space between the two winds, upon the pillar, I invoke, establish, and bow to the eight most excellent Vasus, who are mounted on horses, adorned with flower garlands and the like, endowed with wealth and prosperity, and the upholders of the Vasus. 105.
Come here, O Vasus, and enter into the thirteenth [cup].
Om, you are the purifier of the Vasu, with a hundred streams; you are the purifier of the Vasu, with a thousand streams.
May Savitṛ purify you with the filter of Vasu, the hundred-streamed, well-formed, and desire-yielding.
Om Bhūr Bhuvaḥ Svaḥ! O Vasus, come hither and stay.
May you accept this worship arising from the sixteen substances; homage to you!
(108) In the wind-pillar, I invoke, establish, and bow down to Kubera, the giver of wealth, who is accompanied by yakṣas, who has a human vehicle, and who wields a mace. (109)
Come here, O Giver of Wealth, and enter that fourteenth pillar:
"Oṃ! We, maintaining our minds within your bodies through the vow of Soma, may we be endowed with progeny; may we be possessed of splendor. (2.148.110)
Oṃ bhūr bhuvaḥ svaḥ! O Dhanada, come here and remain here!
Accept this worship consisting of sixteen articles; salutations to you!
[To] Bṛhaspati, the Guru, who resides upon the pillar situated in the intermediate space between Vāyu and the North. 111–112.
I invoke, I establish, I bow to the treasure-house of speech.
O Bṛhaspati, come hither; enter the fifteenth pillar.
Om! O Bṛhaspati, that which is beyond the reach of the enemy, which is glorious, radiant, and possessed of wisdom among men...
O you who have shone forth by your own power, born of the Cosmic Order (Ṛta), bestow upon us that wonderful wealth.
Om Bhūr Bhuvaḥ Svaḥ! O Bṛhaspati, come here and remain;
accept this worship consisting of sixteen articles; salutations unto you. 11.4–5.
In the pillar situated between the north and the northeast, I invoke, establish, and bow down to Viśvakarman,
who possesses great splendor, who is white, rich in the arts of craftsmanship, omniscient, and eternal. (116)
Come here, O Viśvakarman; enter into this sixteen-pillared pillar.
(117) Oṃ! O Viśvakarman, by means of this strengthening oblation, you made Indra the protector and strengthened him.
To him the ancient people bowed down, so that he might be formidable and worthy of invocation. (118)
"O Bhūḥ Bhuvaḥ Svaḥ, Viśvakarman, come here and stay!
Accept this worship consisting of sixteen articles; salutations to you!
O Rādhikā, in this manner one should worship the sixteen pillars made of earth.
"Whatever the Blessed Lord Kṛṣṇa has said, that has been declared by me here.

Thus ends the one hundred and forty-eighth chapter, titled "Description of the Invocation and Worship of the Deities in the Sixteen Pillars of the Pavilion for the Sixty-four Yoginīs and Fifty Kṣetrapālas," within the section on the Establishment of Deities in the second part, the Tretā-Santāna, of the *Śrī Lakṣmī-Nārāyaṇīya Saṃhitā*.

Chapter 150 → Śrī Kṛṣṇa said:
Listen, O Rādhikā! I shall tell you what the Blessed Puruṣottama spoke later on to the devotee Devāyatana; I speak it to you. 1.
"Oṃ, obeisance to Nāgamātṛ," with these words one should worship the sacrificial wood chips.
One should offer sandalwood paste, flowers, incense, a lamp, and food offerings.
(2) With the mantra "Oṃ, obeisance to all," one should worship the tying of the branch;
one should offer sandalwood paste, flowers, incense, a lamp, and food offerings. (3)

Having emerged from the western gate, one should worship the auspicious archway (toraṇa) of the eastern gate, located exactly one cubit outside the pavilion to the east. This archway, known as "the very firm," should be made of *aśvattha* wood and colored like vermilion. 4.
One should indeed worship [the gate] adorned with Mount Mahendra and marked with conch shells.
(5) Oṃ! Protect this sacrifice and guard it well;
ward off all obstacles here. I bow to you who stand firm. (6)
Oṃ, I praise Agni, the domestic priest, the divine ministrant of the sacrifice,
the invoker, the bestower of jewels— protect the purposeful pavilion!
(7) Oṃ, to the one presided over by the Ṛgveda and to the one with very firm thighs!
Salutations to you, O Sudṛḍhatoraṇa; I invoke you, salutations! 8.
O Dṛḍhatoraṇa, accept the perfume, flowers, incense, lamps, food offering, fruit, water, betel leaf, and the sacrificial fee; salutations to you! 9.
Oṃ, here he abides; salutations again and again to the Kṛta Yuga. I invoke the Kṛta Yuga at the archway; salutations to you.
2.149.10. [I offer] fragrance, flowers, incense, lamps, food offerings, fruit, and water.
"Accept the betel leaf and the sacrificial fee; salutations to you in the Satya Yuga. 11. "In that very place, salutations to Rāhu; I invoke Rāhuka.
[I offer] fragrance, flowers, incense, lamps, food offerings, fruit, and water. 12.
"O Rāhu, accept the betel-leaf and the sacrificial fee; salutations to you, O deity!
Salutations to Bṛhaspati; I invoke Bṛhaspati.
[I offer] perfume, flowers, incense, lamps, food offerings, fruit, and water."
"Accept the betel and the sacrificial fee, O Bṛhaspati, and salutations to you.
(14) Having placed one water-pot there and touched the earth, he should recite the mantra:
"Oṃ! May Heaven and Earth sprinkle this sacrifice for us. (15)
Fulfill us with provisions; make us prosperous with juices and the like.
Therein, the medicinal herbs (*oṣadhayaḥ*) are to be scattered, and barley (*yavāḥ*) is to be scattered, following the *mantra*:
"Oṃ! The medicinal herbs converse together with Soma, the King. (16)
O King, we cause that person for whom the Brāhmaṇa performs [this rite] to cross over [to safety].
(17) Then, having placed the water-pot upon the ground, one should recite the mantra as follows: "Om! Smell the pot; may the drops enter into thee, O Great One. (18)
Return again with vigor; may you yield a thousandfold.
May wealth, flowing in broad streams and rich in milk, enter me once more.
(19) Having filled the pitcher with water and remembered the sacred ford (*tīrtha*), one should recite the mantra.
Oṃ! You are the upholding of Varuṇa; you are the supports of Varuṇa’s pillar.
(2.149.20) You are the seat of Varuṇa’s cosmic order (*ṛta*); you are the dwelling-place of Varuṇa’s cosmic order.
Sit upon the seat of Varuṇa’s cosmic order; become the immortal essence of all sacred fords (*tīrtha*). (21)

Then one should cast fragrance into the jar and into the waters of the sacred fords: Oṃ! I invoke here Śrī, the goddess of all beings, who is the gateway of fragrance, invincible, eternally nourishing, and the bestower of prosperity. (22)
Then, reciting the mantras for those herbs, one should scatter all the medicinal plants there:
"Oṃ! Those herbs which went forth to the gods in the three ages of old;
I invoke the hundred and seven abodes of the tawny ones. (24)
Then, reciting the mantra of the *dūrvā* grass, one should scatter *dūrvā* blades there:
"Oṃ! From joint to joint it grows, from node to node it rises.
Even so, O *dūrvā*, spread forth for us with a thousandfold and a hundredfold. (25)
Then, reciting that mantra, one should cast five sprouts there:
Oṃ! Your seat is in the *aśvattha* tree; your dwelling is made upon its leaf.
You shall indeed be sharers of cattle, if you save the man. (27)
Then, reciting the mantra for them, he should offer seven types of earth:
"Oṃ! Be pleasant to us, O Earth; be free from thorns and a place of rest.
Grant us wide protection and be a giver of nourishment here. (28)
Then one should offer a betel nut while reciting its mantra as well:
Oṃ! Those plants which bear fruit and those which are fruitless, those which have blossoms and those which are flowerless—may they, impelled by Bṛhaspati, release us from sin. (2.149.30)
Then, reciting their respective mantras, one should place exactly five jewels:
"Oṃ! Agni, the wise lord of spoils, has stepped forth toward the oblations;
bestowing jewels upon the donor, bring all jewels hither. (31)

Then, reciting the *Hiraṇyagarbha* hymn, he should cast gold [into the fire]. (32) *oṃ hiraṇyagarbhaḥ samavartatāgre bhūtasya jātaḥ patireka āsīt | sa dādhāra pṛthivīṃ dyāmutemāṃ kasmai devāya haviṣā vidhema ||* (33) Oṃ!
