In the [southern] pit, two followers of the Yajurveda are present, and the Brahmā priest there indeed faces north;
the performer of the *homa* faces east.
Then, in the western pit, there are two twice-born followers of the Sāmaveda, and in the northern pit, two followers of the Atharvaveda.
Likewise, two other reciters (*jāpaka*) and two additional Brahmins (*bhūsura*),
who are knowers of their respective Vedas, should sit according to their seats.
Then the Preceptor (*ācārya*) [should sit] in his own sacrificial pit (*kuṇḍa*) between Indra and Īśāna.
Then the Brahmā priest should sit facing east,

and likewise the Guru, having arrived at his own fire-pit, should establish the sacred fire according to the procedure prescribed in his own Gṛhya-sūtra; others [should do so] in their five pits in the same manner.
And they should perform the installation of the fire in a single sacrificial pit (kuṇḍa) according to the rules.
The preceptor (ācārya) should sit facing east, and the Brahman priest facing north.
First, the patron of the sacrifice (yajamāna) should indeed perform the worship of the sacrificial pit.
Having himself sat down to the south of the fire’s hearth,
and the preceptor having likewise sat down to the west of the sacrificial pit,
he should then perform the ritual sipping of water (ācamana), restrain his breaths (prāṇāyāma), and speak as follows.
"May those beings depart who dwell upon the earth;
may those beings who cause obstacles go far away from the site of the sacrifice.
Having scattered mustard seeds and sprinkled the pavilion with the five products of the cow (pañcagavya), [he should perform the rite].
One should offer salutations to the preceptors regarding the sacrificial pit and the ritual materials;
having also prostrated before Gaṇeśa and taken unbroken rice grains (*akṣata*) and other items in hand,
one should announce the place and the time, along with the perfumes, flowers, water, and so forth.
Therefore, with devotion, I shall perform this rite for the consecration of the temple of the deity (15),
as well as the installation of the fire and its ancillary acts such as the purification;
likewise, the installation and worship of the deities of the girdle and the womb (16).
Then, having swept the site of the fire and sprinkled the sacrificial pit (*kuṇḍa*) with water mixed with *kuśa* grass,
one should take flowers in both hands and touch the pit,
saying: "I invoke that pit fashioned by Viśvakarman."
And that divine, wondrous bodily abode of yours which is presided over by Agni;
and those gods who reside in the sacrificial pit, and those deities who are at the front of the pit—
may they all, being composed, grant prosperity and the successful completion of the sacrifice.
"May Kuṇḍa grant us the desired success of the sacrifice, which is beneficial.
Having prayed thus, one should worship Viśvakarmā in the center of the sacrificial pit:
"Oṃ Viśvakarman! By means of this strengthening oblation, you made Indra our protector, one who cannot be slain."
To him the ancient tribes bowed down, for he was indeed formidable and worthy of invocation.
(21) You are taken with a support; I take you for Indra Viśvakarman.
This is your resting place; I offer you for Indra Viśvakarman. Om, obeisance! (22)
Having worshipped with sandalwood paste and other offerings, one should pray for the purification of the excavation:
"Obeisance to you; destroy all defects of the pit, whether known or unknown!";
then, upon the white girdle, one should invoke Śrī Viṣṇu.
Oṃ, O Viṣṇu, for the sake of protecting the sacrifice, be present in the sacrificial pit.
(24) Oṃ, Viṣṇu strode across this; he planted his foot in three places.
His footprint is gathered in the white [space]; Svāhā! I worship the Wielder of the Discus. (25)
Having worshipped Śrī Hari Viṣṇu, [one should say] "Obeisance, obeisance to Mekhalā. Then, having worshipped the white Mekhalā and others, as well as the middle one which is red,
one should invoke Brahmā there while reciting the mantra.
Seated upon a swan, for the sake of protecting the sacrifice, be present in this sacrificial pit (kuṇḍa).
Om! Brahmā revealed the primordial knowledge from the east, the far-reaching, radiant light from the boundless.
The foundations of this world are his highest stations;
he is the womb of both the existent and the non-existent.
Having thus worshipped Brahmā, [one should say]: "Salutations again and again to the girdle."
The sacrificer should worship the red girdle presided over by Brahmā.
Then, upon the black girdle below that, he should invoke Rudra himself—
the bull-mounted, bearer of the Gaṅgā, and wielder of the Pināka bow.
Come, O Blessed Lord Rudra; be present in this sacrificial pit.
*Oṃ*, salutations to you, O Rudra, who possesses the mind; and likewise salutations to your arrow.
Salutations to your two arms, and salutations to your girdle. Salutations, salutations!
The sacrificer should worship Rudradevī, who is dark-complexioned and wears a girdle.
In a triangular, circular, hexagonal, lotus-shaped, or eight-cornered pit, the yoni should be joined;
it should be at the western end, with its tip facing eastward.
In a corner pit or a yoni-shaped pit, a [separate] yoni should not be made in any case.
It should have a depth equal to half the area of the field (*kṣetra*), a length equal to one part of the field,
and its upper edge should be twenty-four parts high, with a girdle (*mekhalā*) that is slightly sloped toward the front.
Having entered the fire-pit (kuṇḍa), she is endowed with two hemispheres;
her base is broad, her central stalk is even, and her form is like a leaf of the holy fig tree (aśvattha).
She, whose nature is the primordial support (brahmādhāna), is indeed to be worshipped within the pit. || 35-36 ||
Homage to you, the cause of the world, and homage to you, the sustainer of Brahmā!
Oṃ, you are the source of all, and you are also the navel of all.
I worship you with perfumes and other offerings; I pray for the attainment of my desired goal.
"Salutations to You, the womb of Brahma, who bestows happiness and unites embodied beings with the goals of human existence within the womb of Brahman.
Having thus worshipped the Yoni, one should then perform the worship of the throat. (38–39)
I invoke Sragdhara, the support of the head. The blue-necked, dark-throated Rudras have taken refuge in heaven;
we bow to their bows that extend for a thousand yojanas.
Having thus worshipped with perfumes and other offerings, one should pray to the radiant throat:
"O auspicious one, you reside in the pit of the throat, and the girdle stands all around you.
Then, one should worship the navel, which resembles the pit or the lotus.
I invoke the Navel, the foundation of all sacrificial pits.
My navel is consciousness of the mind; my anus is honor and ash.
My testicles are joy and procreation; my vulva is good fortune and offspring.
"By your two shanks and feet, you are Dharma, the King established in the people.
Having thus worshipped [her], and having prayed, "O Nābhī, may you remain in this small vessel together with the gods;
be the source of auspicious prosperity," he then bowed down once more.
One should worship Vāstupuruṣa in the southwest corner of the sacrificial pit (kuṇḍa).
Taking flowers, one should say: "I invoke Vāstu; I worship Vāstu. Oṃ, O Lord of the Dwelling (Vāstoṣpati), acknowledge us!
Be easy of access and free from disease for us;
whatever we entreat of you, grant that to us.
Be auspicious to our bipeds and auspicious to our quadrupeds. 47.
I offer fragrance, flowers, incense, lamps, and food offerings;
I also present a bali-oblation to the one who is the form of Vāstupuruṣa—
the man who is the son of Brahmā, the son of Rudra, and the refuge of all the gods.
Having bowed to Vāstu, the sacrificer should then establish the fire in due order;
likewise, he may do so in a sacrificial pit (kuṇḍa) free from husks, hair, charcoal, and the like,
or on a sacrificial mound (sthaṇḍila), having swept the square ground with excellent *kuśa* grass.
Having cast *kuśa* grass toward the northeast and smeared [the ground] with cow-dung water,
one should scratch a line approximately one span long from west to east using either a wooden sword (*sphya*) or the base of a sacrificial ladle (*sruva*).
Then, in that same manner, one should scratch three lines in successive order from south to north.
Having scooped up earth with the ring finger and thumb in the same order as the previous scraping,
and having sprinkled it with water, [he should place] the fire in a bronze vessel,
covered by another bronze vessel, facing westward.
Having established [the fire] and worshipped it with the Gāyatrī mantra:
"Oṃ bhūr bhuvaḥ svaḥ; we meditate upon that most excellent splendor of the divine Savitṛ;
may he inspire our intellects," and I also worship the Fire.
Oṃ, may we know Nārāyaṇa; may we meditate upon Vāsudeva.
May that Viṣṇu inspire us. I bow to and contemplate the Fire.
Then, one should establish the fire in the sacrificial pit (kuṇḍa) by way of the womb (yonimārga). 55–56.
Reciting, "Oṃ, Agni is the head of heaven, the summit, the lord of this earth;
he quickens the seeds of the waters," one should cause [the fire] to be established.
And for the sake of maintaining the life of the fire, one should offer some fuel-sticks.

One should then pour water and other substances into the fire-vessel; this indeed brings auspiciousness. (58) One should perform the extraction [of the fire] from the preceptor’s pit into the other pits, establish the fire, and offer oblations; thereafter, one should perform the worship of the nine planets. (59)
In the northeast, upon the household pedestal, one should perform the invocation of the nine planets.
In the center, within a circular area, one should invoke the Sun facing east with red flowers and unbroken rice grains,
and establish him while reciting the mantra.
Oṃ bhūr bhuvaḥ svaḥ! O Sūrya, come here and remain here.
(61) Oṃ! Moving through the dark space, establishing both the immortal and the mortal, the divine Savitṛ comes on his golden chariot, beholding all the worlds. (62)
I pay homage to Sūrya and worship him with perfumes, flowers, and other offerings. In the southeast, upon a wheel resembling a half-moon,
one should invoke, meditate upon, and worship Candra with white flowers and unbroken grains of rice, using sandalwood and other substances.
Oṃ bhūr bhuvaḥ svaḥ! O Moon, come here and remain here.
Oṃ! O gods, bestow this man upon me as one without rivals, for great sovereignty, for great preeminence, for great lordship over the people, and for the power of the senses.
"This one is the son of so-and-so, the son of so-and-so; he belongs to this people. Yonder is King Soma, the king of us Brāhmaṇas. Om, obeisance! (66).
In the southern triangle, however, [one should worship] with red flowers, unbroken rice grains (*akṣata*), and other offerings.
One should invoke and worship Bhauma facing the south.
Oṃ bhūr bhuvaḥ svaḥ, O Bhauma, come here and stay here!
Oṃ, Agni is the head of heaven, the summit, the lord of this earth. 68.
He quickens the seeds of the waters; *Oṃ*, salutations again and again to the one of the earth.
In the northeast, within a circle resembling an arrow, facing north, one should invoke and worship Budha with beautiful yellow flowers and unbroken rice grains.
Oṃ bhūrbhuvaḥ svaḥ! O Budha, come here and stay! (2.150.70) Oṃ! Awaken! Be vigilant in your dreams!
Having performed sacrifices and works of public utility, you have created this world and its well-being.
In this assembly hall, upon the higher [seat], may all the gods and the sacrificer sit down.
(7.1) Upon the northern and the square mandala, facing north...
One should invoke Bṛhaspati with yellow flowers and unbroken grains (akṣata) and bow to him:
"Oṃ bhūr bhuvaḥ svaḥ! O Bṛhaspati, come here and stay!
I worship the Guru with perfumes, flowers, and other offerings while reciting the mantra. (72–73)

Oṃ! O Bṛhaspati, that which surpasses the enemy, which is worthy of honor, which shines brilliantly and possesses wisdom among men—that splendor born of truth, which has shone forth, bestow that wonderful wealth upon us. (74) And in the eastern pentagonal mandala, [one should worship] the Sage facing eastward.
One should invoke and worship Śukra with white flowers and rice-grains:
"Oṃ bhūr bhuvaḥ svaḥ! O Śukra, come here and remain here!
Accept the fragrance, flowers, incense, and so forth; I bow to you. (75–76)
Oṃ. From food, the essence that flows forth, Prajāpati—the Kṣatra—drank with the Brahman: milk, Soma, truth, power, the drink of the wise, the bright essence of the plant.
This milk, nectar, and honey is the very power (*indriya*) of Indra.
But in the western mandala, which is shaped like a bow, one should face westward, invoke Saturn with black flowers and unbroken rice grains (*akṣata*), and worship him. (77–78)
Oṃ bhūr bhuvaḥ svaḥ! O Śani, come here and remain here!
Oṃ! May the divine waters be auspicious for our well-being and for our drinking.
May they flow toward us for peace and prosperity. I worship and I bow down to them.

In the southwest, upon a winnowing-basket-shaped mandala facing south, one should invoke and worship Rāhu with black flowers and unbroken grains (akṣata). "Oṃ bhūr bhuvaḥ svaḥ! O Rāhu, come here and stay! (81)
Oṃ! With what [aid] has the wonderful one become our friend, he who ever increases [us]?
With what most powerful turn of events do I worship and bow?
(82) And in the northwest, within a banner-shaped maṇḍala, [he faces] southward.
One should invoke and worship the deity Ketu with incense, flowers, and unbroken grains (akṣata).
Oṃ bhūrbhuvaḥ svaḥ! O Ketu, come here and stay here!
Oṃ! Making a banner for one who has no banner, and a form for the formless mortal. (RV 10.85.20)
You were born from the *samuṣads*; I honor you and bow to you.
Now I invoke and establish the presiding deities (*adhidevatās*).
The deities are to be established facing the Sun, with Ravi in the center. (85)
On the right side, one should invoke Rudra with white flowers and unbroken rice grains:
"Oṃ bhūr bhuvaḥ svaḥ! O Rudra, come here and stay here!
Oṃ, we worship Tryambaka, the fragrant one who increases prosperity. (86–87)
"May I be released from death as a cucumber from its stalk, yet not be released from immortality.
In the southeast and toward the right of the moon, one should invoke, establish, and worship Umā with red flowers,
unbroken rice grains, sandalwood, and other offerings.
Oṃ bhūr bhuvaḥ svaḥ! O Umā, come here and stay here!
Oṃ! Śrī and Lakṣmī are your two wives; day and night are your two sides; the stars are your form, and the Aśvins are your open mouth.
"Granting [desires], grant [them] to me; grant [them] to all the world, grant [them] to Umā. Homage to Umā! (2.150.90).
To the south, on the right of Bhauma, [one should worship] with yellow flowers, unbroken rice, and other offerings.
One should invoke Skanda, worship him, offer oblations to him, and meditate upon him.
Oṃ bhūrbhuvaḥ svaḥ! O Skanda, come here and stay here!
Accept the perfume, flowers, incense, lamps, food offerings, and so forth.
Oṃ! When you first cried out at birth, whether rising from the ocean or from the primordial waters,
with the wings of a hawk and the forelegs of a deer.
O steed, you are great-born and worthy of praise.
(93) To the northeast, one should invoke Viṣṇu with yellow flowers and unbroken grains, saying:
"Bhūr bhuvaḥ svaḥ! O Viṣṇu, come hither and stay! (94)
Oṃ, Viṣṇu strode across this; in three places he planted his step.
It is gathered in his footstep-dust, Svāhā! And obeisance to Viṣṇu.
Then, to the north of the Guru and to the south [of the disciple], one should [worship] Aja with white flowers and unbroken rice grains (akṣata).

One should invoke [the deity] with: "Bhūr bhuvaḥ svaḥ! O Brahman, come and be present! (96). "Oṃ! The primordial wisdom of Brahman, from the beginning, has shone forth from the radiant expanse beyond the horizon.
He has revealed its foundations, its highest manifestations, and the source of both the existent and the non-existent. (97)
In the east, on the right side of Śukra, one should invoke Hari with yellow flowers and unhusked grain, saying:
"Bhūr bhuvaḥ svaḥ! O Indra, come and stay! [And:
"Oṃ, Indra the protector, Indra the savior..."
I invoke the easily-invoked, heroic Indra; I call upon Śakra, Indra, who is invoked by many.
May the bounteous Indra bestow well-being upon us. 99.
In the west, to the right of Śani, one should invoke Yama with black flowers and unbroken rice grains (akṣata), saying:
"Bhūr bhuvaḥ svaḥ! O Yama, come and stay!
[Oṃ] "To Yama thee, to Makha thee, to the heat of the Sun thee!"
"O Deva, may Savitṛ truly protect you from the touch of the earth at night.
You are the flame, you are the radiance, you are the heat; homage to Yama!
And [one should worship] Kāla in the south and southwest of Rāhu with smoky-colored flowers and unbroken grains."
One should invoke [the water]: "Bhūr bhuvaḥ svaḥ! O Kāla, come and stay!
"Oṃ! You are the furrow; I draw you up from the earth of the ocean. "The waters have united with the waters, the plants with the plants. O Kāla, homage to you!"
In the northwest, to the right of Ketu, one should invoke Citragupta with red flowers, unbroken rice, and other offerings:
"Come here, O Citragupta, and remain! Om Bhūr Bhuvaḥ Svaḥ, O Citrāvasu, may prosperity be yours; may I reach the further shore. (104–105)
"O Rādhā, 'I worship'—this indeed is the worship of the presiding deities (adhidevatās).
That which Śrī Hari spoke to His devotee has been related by Me.

Thus ends the one hundred and fiftieth chapter, titled "The Description of the Installation of the Fire, the Altar (kuṇḍa), the Deities of the Girdle (mekhalā), the Source of Fire (devayoni), the Worship of the Fire, the Worship of the Nine Planets (navagrahas), and the Worship of the Presiding Deities," in the second section, the Tretā-santāna, of the *Śrī Lakṣmī-Nārāyaṇīya Saṃhitā*.

Śrī Kṛṣṇa said:
Listen, O Rādhikā, to that which Hari spoke to Devakī;
I shall now describe to you the invocation of the presiding deities and other rites.
In the center, to the left of the sun, with red flowers, unbroken rice, and other offerings, one should recite:
"Oṃ bhūr bhuvaḥ svaḥ, I invoke Agni; come and be present!
(2) "Oṃ, I place Agni at the forefront as my messenger; I address him, the bearer of oblations."
O Agni, I invoke the gods here; I worship you with reverence.
(3) In the south-eastern direction and to the left of the moon, [I offer] water with white flowers and unbroken rice grains:
"Oṃ bhūr bhuvaḥ svaḥ! I summon the water; come and stay here! (4)
Oṃ, O Agni, you have taken your seat within the waters; you take root within the plants.
Being born again in their womb, I worship you with water; salutations to you!
(5) On the southern side, at the location of Bhauma, one should worship the Earth with red flowers and unbroken grains (akṣata).
Oṃ bhūr bhuvaḥ svaḥ! O Earth, I summon you; come here and remain. (6) Oṃ! Be pleasant to us, O Earth, free from thorns, providing a secure dwelling.
Grant us wide-spreading shelter; O Earth, I worship you, homage to you! (7)
In the northeast and to the left of Budha, one should worship Viṣṇu with yellow flowers and unbroken grains (akṣata):
Oṃ bhūr bhuvaḥ svaḥ! O Viṣṇu, I invoke you; come here and stay! Oṃ! Viṣṇu strode across this universe; he has indeed placed his foot in three places.
I worship that which is gathered in your dust, O Viṣṇu; salutations to you!
(9) To the north and to the left of the Guru, one should worship Indra with yellow flowers and unbroken grains:
"Oṃ bhūr bhuvaḥ svaḥ! O Indra, I summon you; come and stay! (2.151.10)
Oṃ! O Indra, being well-pleased and accompanied by the Maruts, drink the Soma, O wise hero, slayer of Vṛtra.
Slay the enemies, drive away the adversaries, and then grant us fearlessness.
Make [us] secure on every side.
(11) To the east, with white flowers and unbroken grains of rice, [one should invoke] Śacī:
"Oṃ bhūrbhuvaḥ svaḥ! O Indrāṇī, I summon you; come hither and be established here. (12)
Oṃ, you are the girdle of Aditi, the turban of Indrāṇī.
You are Pūṣan; shine for the sake of the Gharma. O Indrāṇī, I worship you; salutations to you!
(13) [One should worship] Prajāpati with white flowers and unbroken rice grains behind and to the left of Śani.
Oṃ bhūr bhuvaḥ svaḥ! O Prajāpati, I summon you; come here and remain present. (14) Oṃ! Prajāpati, no one other than you has encompassed all these forms.
Whatever desire we have while offering this oblation to you, may that be ours; may we become masters of riches. (15)
To the left of Rāhu, in the southwest (nairṛtya), one should invoke the Nāga with black flowers and unbroken rice grains:
"Oṃ bhūr bhuvaḥ svaḥ! O Nāga, I invoke you; come here and remain!
Oṃ, salutations to the serpents, whichever ones dwell upon the earth.
To those who are in the intermediate space and those who are in heaven, I offer worship to you; salutations!
|| 17 || And to the left of the banner, in the north-western direction, one should invoke the goat with white flowers and unbroken grains:
"Oṃ bhūr bhuvaḥ svaḥ, O Brahmā, I summon you; come and stay! || 18 ||
Oṃ. Brahmā first revealed the knowledge from the east; from the boundless, the radiant Vena brought it forth.
He disclosed its foundations, its highest forms, and the source of both the existent and the non-existent.
(1.9) Then, one should invoke the five world-protectors, the excellent guardians.
In the northwest and the north, [one should worship] Rāhu with yellow flowers, unbroken rice grains (*akṣata*), and so forth.
"Oṃ bhūr bhuvaḥ svaḥ! I invoke Gaṇeśa; come here and stay!
Having worshipped you with perfumes, flowers, unbroken rice grains, and food offerings, I bow down to you. (2.151.21)
Oṃ! We invoke you, the Lord of hosts, among all hosts;
we invoke you, the Lord of the beloved, among all that is dear; we invoke you, the Lord of treasures, among all treasures.
O Vāsava, I bow to Gaṇeśa.
(22) "I am the one who has entered the womb; you are the one who has entered the womb.
In the north, west, and south, [one should worship] Durgā with red flowers and unbroken grains of rice. (23)
Oṃ bhūrbhuvaḥ svaḥ! O Durgā, I summon you; come and stay.
I worship you, I bow to you; grant happiness to the people; obeisance! Oṃ jātavedase sunavāma...
The Veda drives away the one who acts with hostility;
may he, like Agni, carry us across all difficulties and beyond all evils, as a boat carries one across the sea. 25.
In the center [one should worship] Sūrya, and to the north, Vāyu, with yellow flowers, unbroken rice, and other offerings:
"Oṃ bhūr bhuvaḥ svaḥ! O Vāyu, come here and stay here!
Oṃ ā no niyudbhiḥ śatinībhiḥ... [etc.]
Come to this sacrifice with thousands of [horses] that bear you;
O Vāyu, rejoice at this libation!
Do you all protect us always with blessings. 27.
In the east, in the eastern part of the Śukra [mandala], one should invoke the space with blue flowers:
"Oṃ bhūrbhuvaḥ svaḥ! O Space, come here and remain here!
(28) "Oṃ! Drink the ghee, you drinkers of ghee; drink the fat!"
O purifiers, drink! You are the oblation of the intermediate space; *svāhā*!
To the quarters, the intermediate quarters, the primary quarters, the secondary quarters, and the upward quarters—from all the quarters, *svāhā*! I honor and I bow down. 29.
To the south and southwest of Rāhu, with white flowers, unbroken rice, and other offerings:
Oṃ bhūr bhuvaḥ svaḥ! O Aśvins, come here; stay here!
Oṃ! That whip of yours which is honey-sweet, O Aśvins, and full of truth—
I honor the Aśvins, who desire to partake in the sacrifice.
Having offered incense, lamps, and food offerings to the gods, I bow down to them.
Then, the performer of the sacrifice should invoke Indra and the other deities in the cardinal directions, beginning with the east.
In the east: Oṃ bhūrbhuvaḥ svaḥ, O Indra, come here and stay!
I worship you with perfumes and other offerings; I remember you and I bow to you.
(33) In the southeast: Oṃ bhūrbhuvaḥ svaḥ, O Agni, come here and stay!
I worship with perfumes and other offerings, I remember you, and I bow to you.
(34) To the south: Oṃ bhūr bhuvaḥ svaḥ! Yama, come here and stay!
I worship you with perfumes and other offerings, I remember you, and I bow to you. (35)
In the southwest: Oṃ bhūr bhuvaḥ svaḥ, O Nirṛti, come and stay!
I worship you with perfumes and other offerings, I remember you, and I bow to you.
(36) In the west: Oṃ bhūr bhuvaḥ svaḥ, O Varuṇa, come and stay!
I worship with perfumes and other offerings, I remember [you], and I bow down.
|| 37 || In the northwest: *Oṃ bhūr bhuvaḥ svaḥ*, O Vāyu, come and stay!
I worship with perfumes and other offerings, I remember [you], and I bow down. || 38 ||
In the north: Oṃ bhūr bhuvaḥ svaḥ, Kubera, come and stay!
I worship you with perfumes and other offerings; I remember you and I bow to you.
(39) In the northeast: Oṃ bhūr bhuvaḥ svaḥ, Īśāna, come and stay!
I worship with perfumes and other offerings, I remember [thee], and I bow down.
(2.151.40) Between the northeast and the east, I invoke Brahmā:
"Oṃ bhūr bhuvaḥ svaḥ! O Brahmā, come here and stay! (41)
I worship with perfumes and other offerings, I remember, and I bow down.
Between the directions of Nirṛti and Varuṇa, I invoke Ananta and I praise him.
Oṃ bhūr bhuvaḥ svaḥ! O Ananta, come here and remain here.
I worship with perfumes and other offerings, I remember [you], and I bow down.
(43) Then, one should invoke Brahmā and the others situated in the center of the maṇḍala:
"Oṃ bhūr bhuvaḥ svaḥ! O Brahmā, come here and remain! (44)
I worship with perfumes and other offerings, I remember you, and I bow down to you.
Oṃ bhūr bhuvaḥ svaḥ! O Śiva, come here and remain here.
I worship with perfumes and other offerings, I remember you, and I bow down to you.
Oṃ bhūr bhuvaḥ svaḥ! O Viṣṇu, come here and remain here.
I worship you with perfumes and other offerings; I remember you and I bow to you.
Oṃ bhūr bhuvaḥ svaḥ! O Gaṇapati, come here and remain here.
I worship with perfumes and other offerings, I remember you, and I bow down to you.
Oṃ bhūr bhuvaḥ svaḥ! O Lakṣmī, come here and remain here.
I worship with perfumes and other offerings, I remember you, and I bow down to you.
Oṃ! The five rivers flow into the Sarasvatī with their currents.
That river Sarasvatī indeed became fivefold in that region.
Oṃ Bhūr Bhuvaḥ Svaḥ! O Sarasvatī, come here and stay here. (2.151.50)
I worship her with perfumes and other offerings, I remember her, and I bow to her:
"Oṃ! O Ambā, O Ambikā, O Ambālikā! No one leads me away.
The horse has been well-fed; [go] to Śubhadrikā, the dweller of Kāmpīla. (51)
Oṃ bhūr bhuvaḥ svaḥ! O Durgā, come here and stay here!
I worship you with perfumes and other offerings; I remember you and I bow to you.
Oṃ bhūr bhuvaḥ svaḥ! O Kṣetrapāla, come here and stay here! 52–53.
I worship with perfumes and other offerings, I remember [you], and I bow down.
Oṃ bhūr bhuvaḥ svaḥ! O beings, come here and stay!
I worship with perfumes and other offerings, I remember [you], and I bow down.
Oṃ bhūr bhuvaḥ svaḥ! O Viśvakarman, come here and remain here.
I worship you with perfumes and other offerings; I remember you and I bow to you.
Having proclaimed the place and time, for the sake of the supreme success of the sacrifice. || 55-56 ||
I perform worship for all the gods with sandalwood and other offerings.
Oṃ, obeisance to the nine planets beginning with the Sun; may you grant us peace.
Oṃ, obeisance to the deities beginning with Rudra; may you grant us protection.
Om, salutations to the deities beginning with Agni; for you are the bestowers of splendor upon us.

Om, salutations to the guardians of the worlds beginning with Gaṇeśa; for you are the granters of our desires. Om, salutations to the guardians of the directions beginning with Indra; for you are indeed the bestowers of nourishment upon us.
"Salutations to those beginning with Brahmā and ending with Viśvakarman, the bestowers of prosperity.
Having thus worshipped them, the sacrificer, near the sacrificial altar of the planets,
should offer oblations upon the ground with the respective name-mantras as follows:
To Sūrya, jaggery-rice; to Soma, milk-porridge with ghee (61).
To Maṅgala, lentil-rice; to Budha, milk-rice;
to Guru, curd-rice; and to Śukra, rice with ghee (62).
Having offered sesame flour to Śani, milk-rice (pāyasa) to Rāhu,
rice mixed with various condiments (citraudana) to Ketu, and milk-rice as an oblation (bali) to the others,
the performer of the sacrifice should then place a water-pot (kalaśa) in the northeast corner.
One should perform the touching of the earth with the mantra *oṃ bhūr asi*.
With the mantra *oṃ dhānyam asi*, the performer of the sacrifice should scatter grain upon the ground.
With the mantra *om ājighra*, one should place the water-pot upon the grain. (64–65)
With the mantra "oṃ varuṇasya," one should fill the water-vessel with water;
with the mantra "oṃ vasoḥ pavitre," one should wrap a cloth around its neck;
and with the mantra "oṃ yāḥ phalinī," one should offer a betel nut.
With the mantra *oṃ parivāja*, one should cast the five jewels.
(67) With the mantra *oṃ hiraṇyagarbha*, one should offer gold.
With the mantra *oṃ gandhadvārā*, one should offer perfume and the other [substances]. (68)

Reciting the mantra "oṃ yā oṣadhīḥ," one should cast all medicinal herbs together. Having brought earth from a horse stable, an elephant stable, an anthill, a confluence of rivers, a lake, a royal gate, and a cow-pen, one should deposit it [into the vessel].
One should cast *durvā* grass into the water-pot while reciting "oṃ kāṇḍātkāṇḍāt... (2.151.70).
One should cast five types of sprouts while reciting the mantra "oṃ aśvatthe...
One should cast purifying blades of grass while reciting the mantra "oṃ pavitreṇa stha... (71).
With the mantra "oṃ pūrṇā darvī," one should place a vessel of rice into the pitcher.
With the mantra "oṃ śrīśca te," one should place a bilva fruit into the pitcher.
Having thus consecrated the pitcher, one should invoke Varuṇa into the water.
One should invoke Varuṇa with the mantra: *Oṃ tattvāyāmi*.
*Oṃ bhūrbhuvaḥ svaḥ, O Varuṇa, come here and stay!
I worship you and pay homage to you with the sixteen auspicious articles.* (73–74)
May all the oceans, rivers, sacred fords, and lakes,
as well as the clouds that destroy all evils, come together.
All the gods and the purifying fires reside within the water-pot.

With the mantra "kalaśasya mukhe ca," one should consecrate the water-pot (kalaśa). Then, with the "devadānava" mantra, one should pray to the pot. Next follows the worship of the Sarvatobhadra mandala.
One should draw nineteen lines extending toward the northeast.
In the corner, there is a crescent moon (*khaṇḍendu*) consisting of three squares; a chain (*śṛṅkhalā*) consists of five squares;
a creeper (*vallī*) consists of eleven squares; and the auspicious one (*bhadra*) consists of nine squares.
The oblong pond (vāpī) consists of twenty-four squares, and its perimeter is twenty squares.
In the center, an eight-petaled lotus is prescribed with sixteen squares.
The crescent moon is white, the chain is black, and one should fill the creepers with blue.
The pond is auspicious, reddish-brown or white, and its perimeter is yellow in color.
The outer and inner petals are white, while the pericarp is yellow.
The lotus is encircled by a perimeter; outside of it are the qualities of sattva, rajas, and tamas.
In the center of that, one should establish the gods, beginning with Brahmā, as well as the lords of the deities (sureśvaras).
Having proclaimed the place and the time for the rites of establishing the deity,
one should invoke fifty-six deities in the Sarvatobhadra [maṇḍala].
Having taken unbroken grains (akṣata), one should then invoke Brahmā in the center:
"Oṃ bhūr bhuvaḥ svaḥ! O Brahmā, come here and remain here!
I worship you, I remember you, I bow to you; accept this worship! (84)
In the north: Oṃ bhūr bhuvaḥ svaḥ, I invoke Soma;
I worship him, I remember him, I bow to him; come and remain! In the northeast: Oṃ bhūr bhuvaḥ svaḥ, I invoke Īśāna. 85–86.
I worship, I remember, I bow; come and remain!
In the east: Oṃ bhūrbhuvaḥ svaḥ, I invoke Indra.
I worship, I remember, I bow; come and remain!
In the southeast: Oṃ bhūrbhuvaḥ svaḥ, I invoke Agni;
I worship him, I remember him, I bow to him; come and remain!
In the south: Oṃ bhūrbhuvaḥ svaḥ, I invoke Yama.
I worship, I remember, and I bow; come and remain!
In the southwest, Oṃ bhūr bhuvaḥ svaḥ, I invoke Nirṛti.
I worship, I remember, and I bow; come and remain!
In the west: *Oṃ bhūr bhuvaḥ svaḥ, I invoke Varuṇa;
I worship him, I remember him, I bow to him; come and remain!* In the northwest: *Oṃ bhūr bhuvaḥ svaḥ, I invoke Vāyu.*
I worship, I remember, I bow; come and remain!
In the north: Oṃ bhūr bhuvaḥ svaḥ, I invoke Kubera;
I worship, I remember, I bow; come and remain!
In the northeast: "Oṃ bhūr bhuvaḥ svaḥ, I invoke Īśāna;
I worship you, I remember you, I bow to you; come and remain.
Between the northeast and the east, I invoke Brahmā. 94–95.
Oṃ bhūr bhuvaḥ svaḥ! O Brahmā, come here and remain here.
I worship you, I remember you, I bow to you; be the bestower of happiness.
In the space between Vāyu and Soma, I invoke the eight Vasus.
Oṃ bhūr bhuvaḥ svaḥ! O Vasus, come here, stay here!
I worship you, I remember you, I bow to you; may you indeed grant us happiness.
And between Soma and Īśāna, I invoke the Rudras.
Oṃ bhūr bhuvaḥ svaḥ! O Rudras, come here, stay here!
I worship you, I remember you, I bow to you; may you indeed grant us happiness.
Between Īśāna and the East, I invoke the Ādityas.
Oṃ bhūr bhuvaḥ svaḥ! Ādityas, come here, stay here!
2.151.10 0 And I invoke the Aśvins and Kumāra in the region between Indra and Agni:
Oṃ bhūr bhuvaḥ svaḥ! Aśvins, come here, stay here! 10 1
I worship, I remember, and I bow to you, for you two are indeed the givers of happiness to us.
Om! Between Agni and Yama, I invoke the Viśvedevas along with the Pitṛs. Bhūr Bhuvaḥ Svaḥ! O Pitṛs, please remain here.
I worship, I remember, and I bow to them, for they indeed grant us happiness.
(103) And I invoke the Yakṣas between Yama and Nairṛta:
Oṃ bhūr bhuvaḥ svaḥ! O Yakṣas, come hither; stay! (104)
I worship, I remember, and I bow to those who grant us happiness;
I also summon the spirits and *nāgas* dwelling between the regions of Nairṛti and Varuṇa.
Oṃ bhūr bhuvaḥ svaḥ! O spirits, come here, stay here!
I worship, I remember, and I bow down; for they indeed grant us happiness.
Right there, I summon the serpents of the earth, the atmosphere, and the heavens: "Stay!
I worship, I remember, and I bow down; for they indeed grant us happiness."
Between Varuṇa and Vāyu, I worship, remember, and bow down to the Gandharvas and Apsarases, as well as Bhūr, Bhuvar, and Svar.
In that very place, let Bhūr, Bhuvar, Svar, and the Apsarases also abide.
I worship, I remember, and I bow down to those who indeed grant us happiness.
Oṃ! Puñjikasthalī and Kratusthalī are the two Apsarases;
the fangs are their weapon, and the slaughter of men is their missile. Homage be to them! (2.151.110)
Between Brahmā and Soma, I invoke, remember, and bow to Skanda, Śūla, and Nandin.
I worship you in this place; come hither and remain! (111)
Salutations to you, Nandīśvara, Śakra, and Mahākāla.
(1.12) And between Brahmā and Īśāna, [I invoke] the auspicious seven Prajāpatis:
O lords of progeny, Bhūr, Bhuvas, and Svar, come here and remain! (1.13)
I worship, I remember, and I bow to you, for you are the bestower of happiness upon us.
O Durgā, come and remain in the space between Brahmā and Indra.
Bhūr bhuvaḥ svaḥ! I invoke Durgā; I bow to her and I worship her.
To the east of Durgā: "Bhūḥ Bhuvaḥ Svaḥ, I invoke Viṣṇu;
I worship him, I remember him, I bow to him; come and remain!
(1.15) Between Brahmā and Agni: "I invoke the Pitṛs; remain! (1.16)
Bhūr bhuvaḥ svaḥ! O ancestors, come; I worship you.
Between Brahmā and Yama, I summon Death and Diseases.
Om! O Death, go back along that path which is yours... [the rest of the verse].
The other is different from the path of the gods; I speak this to you who have eyes and hear: do not harm our offspring, nor our heroic men. 1.18.18.
I worship, I remember, I bow, come, stay!
And I invoke Gaṇeśa in the space between Brahmā and Nirṛti.
Bhūr bhuvaḥ svaḥ! O Gaṇeśa, come here and stay!
I worship you, I remember you, I bow to you; be the bestower of happiness.
Between Brahmā and Varuṇa, I invoke those called the Waters:
Bhūr, Bhuvaḥ, Svaḥ! O Waters, come here, stay here! 2.151.120–121.
I worship, I remember, and I bow to you, for you are indeed the givers of happiness to us;
and in the space between Brahma and Vayu, I invoke the Maruts.
At the foot of Brahma, I invoke the Earth and I bow to her.
Bhūr bhuvaḥ svaḥ! O Earth, come here and remain here.
I worship you, I remember you, I bow to you; be the bestower of happiness.
Right there, O seven rivers, come here and remain here.
I worship and bow down to Bhūr, Bhuvaḥ, Svaḥ, and the Gaṅgā and other rivers.
O Gaṅgā, Yamunā, Sarasvatī, Śatadrū, and Āpikā;
O Uṣṇā and Asiknī—O seven rivers, I remember you and offer salutations again and again.
Right there, I invoke and bow to the seven oceans:
"O Bhūr, Bhuvar, and Svar, O oceans, come hither and remain!
I worship and remember you, for you are the givers of satisfaction and happiness to us."
"Above that, I invoke the one named Meru: come here and remain! O Meru, you who are Bhūr, Bhuvar, and Svar, I bow to you; be the bestower of happiness upon me.
(128) Now, outside the mandala, in the presence of Soma and the others, in due order:
In the north, however, I invoke and establish the mace:
"Bhūr bhuvaḥ svaḥ! O mace, come here and stay!
In the northeast, I invoke and establish the trident.
Bhūr bhuvaḥ svaḥ! O Trident, come here and stay here.
In the east, I invoke the Vajra, I establish it, and I bow to it.
Bhūr bhuvaḥ svaḥ! O Vajra, come here and stay here.
In the southeast, I invoke Śakti and establish her.
Bhūr bhuvaḥ svaḥ! Come here, arrive at this place, stay; I bow to you.
In the south, I invoke Daṇḍa and establish him. 1.32–1.33.
In the southwest, I invoke and bow to Khaṇḍaheti;
in the west, I invoke and establish Pāśa;
in the northwest, I invoke and establish Aṅkuśa.
"O Bhūr, Bhuvaḥ, and Svaḥ, and you who begin with Daṇḍa, come here and stay!
I worship you, I remember you, and I bow to you, for you are the bestowers of happiness upon us. Outside of that, to the north, I invoke Gautama and I pay homage to him."
I invoke Bhāradvāja in the northeast and bow to him;
I invoke Viśvāmitra in the east and bow to him.
I invoke Kaśyapa in the southeast and bow to him.
In the south, I invoke Jamadagni and bow to him. (138) In the southwest, I invoke Vasiṣṭha and bow to him.
In the west, I call upon Atri, worship him, and bow to him. (139)
In the northwest, I invoke Arundhatī and bow down to her.
In the east, salutations to Indrāṇī; in the southeast, repeated salutations to Kumārī. In the south, salutations to Brāhmī; in the southwest, repeated salutations to Vārāhī.
In the west, salutations to Cāmuṇḍā and Vaiṣṇavī; to Vāyu, salutations! (141) In the north, to Māheśvarī; in the northeast, to Vaināyakī and Śrī.
I worship with salutations and I remember them, for they are indeed the givers of happiness to us. (142)
"Having invoked the fifty-six classes of deities, one should worship them.
Thus spoke Śrī Hari to the devotee Devāyatana. O Rādhā, I have thus declared this to you; the mantras corresponding to those [deities] must be inferred.
One should satisfy the hosts of deities with incense, lamps, and excellent food offerings.

Thus ends the one hundred and fifty-first chapter, titled "The Demonstration of the Invocation of the Pratyadhidevatās, the Lokapālas, the Three Deities and Goddesses, and the Planets; the Installation of the Vessel; the Worship of the Sarvatobhadra Mandala; and the Worship of the Fifty-six Deities," in the second section, the Tretā-santāna, of the glorious *Lakṣmīnārāyaṇīya Saṃhitā*.

Śrī Kṛṣṇa said: O Rādhā, I shall tell you what the Blessed Lord then said to His devotee:
"One should place a copper pitcher upon a lotus in the center of the altar. || 1 ||

Having touched the ground with the mantra "oṃ bhūr asi," having scattered rice or barley grains there, and having placed medicinal herbs with the mantra "sam it," one should then place the water-pot on that spot with the mantra "oṃ ājighra."
Having sprinkled water with the mantra "oṃ varuṇasya... (3), one should wrap [the vessel] with a cloth.
With the mantra "oṃ yāḥ phalinī... (4), one should cast in a betel nut, the five jewels, gold, perfume, and likewise all medicinal herbs.
One should also throw seven types of earth, *dūrvā* grass, and the five-fold sprouts (*pañcapallava*).
One should cast in purifying substances and cause a vessel of rice to be placed there.
Having set down a *śrīphala* fruit and having installed the deity, [one should proceed].
Oṃ bhūr bhuvaḥ svaḥ! O Varuṇa, come here and remain here.
(6) I bow to you and worship you with the sixteen substances; salutations to you. Having made this prayer, one should place the golden image of Nārāyaṇī within his mouth. (7)
Having first performed the rite of transferring the fire and having clothed [the image] in silk garments and other fine fabrics, [he should pray]:
"Come, come, O Blessed Viṣṇu, you who bestow grace upon the worlds!
O Vāsudeva, accept this sacrificial portion; salutations be unto you!"
Oṃ, salutation to Viṣṇu; salutation again and again to Madhusūdana. Oṃ, salutation to Trivikrama and to Vāmana;
Oṃ, salutation to Śrīdhara; Oṃ, salutation to Śrī-Hṛṣīkeśa. (2.152.10)
Salutations to Padmanābha and to Dāmodara; Oṃ, salutations!
To the beginningless Śrī Kṛṣṇa Nārāyaṇa, Oṃ, salutations again and again!
(11) Salutations to Śrī Kṛṣṇa, Oṃ, and salutations to Nārāyaṇa, Oṃ!
"Oṃ, obeisance to Nara-Nārāyaṇa, and Oṃ, obeisance to Hari.
Having worshipped Kṛṣṇa with these names, one should again prostrate. Then the preceptor, having performed the ritual sipping of water (ācamana), should worship the gatekeepers with fragrant scents.
"Recite the hymns, perform the sacrifices, and likewise urge the Brahmins forward.
The preceptor and the officiating priests, having meditated upon the fire in the sacrificial pit, should carry out the ritual according to the rules.
Sitting to the right of each pit, the patron of the sacrifice [should remain there]."
Having taken up kusha grass, barley, and water today at this auspicious time and so forth,
[I offer] this oblation for the purpose of the rite of consecration of the deity; indeed,
this substance is offered to all the planets and likewise to the presiding deities.
And also to the individual presiding deities and to the world-protectors;
likewise to the guardians of the directions, to the triad of gods, and to Gaṇeśa;
as well as to Ambikā, to the hosts of spirits, and to Viśvakarman.
"To Varuṇa, Agni, Vāyu, Sūrya, and Prajāpati," (18) "and also to all the deities beginning with Sviṣṭakṛt—namas, oṃ.
Having uttered this, one should perform the renunciation of the substance for each fire-pit. (19)
While the recitation of the *jāpaka*s is taking place, one should perform the fire-oblation (*homa*).
Having proclaimed the place and the time, one should perform the formal selection (*varaṇa*) with the formula:
"I choose you, such-and-such a Brāhmaṇa, for the office of the Brahman priest."
"I am chosen," he replied; then he performed the prescribed rite.
"I shall act according to my knowledge," [he said]. Then, having moved to the south of the fire, he abandoned the ground intended for the strewing and offered it to the Creator (Vidhātṛ).

Having spread out a seat made of wood from an elephant or similar source and *kuśa* grass with its tips pointing eastward upon that seat, one should personally bring Brahmā for the rite of installation, following the sequence of circumambulation around the fire. (23)
Having addressed him as "O Brahmā," one should cause him to sit upon the seat.
In his absence, however, one should prepare a substitute consisting of fifty kuśa grass blades.
To the north of the fire, two seats should be arranged with kuśa grass blades pointing eastward.
Having fashioned an elephant [shaped vessel] twelve finger-breadths long,
four finger-breadths wide, and with a hollow four finger-breadths deep,
one should place a *camasa* bowl in front of it, held in a vessel in the right hand.

Having filled [the vessel] with water and covered the face of the *brahman* with *kuśa* grass, he should look [at it]; then, to the north of the fire, he should place it upon *kuśa* grass on a western seat. Thereafter, the strewing (*paristaraṇa*) should be performed in the following manner.
Having taken one-fourth of the sacrificial grass (barhis), with four kuśa blades each having their tips pointing eastward,
[he should strew them] from the southeast to the northeast, and from the southwest to the northwest, reaching as far as the Brahma-sthāna and the fire.

The sacrificial grass-strewing (paristaraṇa) is desired to be placed starting from the fire and ending at the *praṇītā* vessel. Having done that, one should then take three blades of *kuśa* grass for the purpose of cutting the *pavitra* to the north-west of the fire.
And for the purpose of purification, one should bring two bunches of *kuśa* grass.
The vessel for the *vāraṇa* water and the *prokṣaṇī* vessel should be twelve finger-breadths in length.
The vessel for the clarified butter (*ājya*) should be made of metal and twelve finger-breadths in width.
Then there is a sacrificial pot (carusthālī) one span high, three blades of *darbha* grass for cleansing,

and the *upayamana* *kuśa* grasses and so forth; also a triad of fuel sticks (*samidh*) made of *pālāśa* wood, each measuring one span, a *sruva* ladle made of *khadira* wood, and a hand-sized vessel.
Clarified butter from a cow, rice grains as the ritual substance, and gold; likewise,
fifty-six and two hundred handfuls of rice,
and a vessel filled with rice— these must be kept protected within the pavilion.
The placing [of the materials] and the cutting of the *darbha* blades for the purifier (*pavitra*) are performed first.
Then, having set aside a distance of one span (*prādeśa*) from the tips with three *kuśa* blades,
one cuts two young *kuśa* shoots to fashion the purifier.
Then, with the pavitra held in his hand, he should sprinkle water from the *praṇītā* vessel into the *prokṣaṇī* vessel using the tips of the ring finger and thumb;
having taken up the two *pavitras* with their tips pointing north, he should likewise sprinkle it three times.
Likewise, the placing of the *prokṣaṇī* vessel in the left hand [should be performed];
then, having taken the two strainers (*pavitra*) with the tip of the ring finger and the thumb,
one should perform the sprinkling three times with the water from the *praṇītā* vessel.
Then follows the sprinkling of the *prokṣaṇī* vessel; thereafter,

having sprinkled each one in sequence— beginning with the *ājyasthālī* (the clarified butter pot) and ending with the *pūrṇapātra* (the full vessel)— one should then sprinkle the *prokṣaṇī* vessel itself.
Having placed [the vessel] in the "non-wandering" space between the two consecrated fires (praṇītāgnī),

and having set down the clarified butter (ājya) that has been prepared in the butter-pot (ājyasthālī) to the east of the fire, he should then, once it has been deposited, pour [the butter] from the caru-pot into it. 42–43.
Having poured out excellent water and set down the prepared rice grains,
the Brahman priest places the clarified butter on the fire, and he himself places it to the north of that.
Then, having likewise placed the sacrificial oblation (caru) simultaneously upon the fire, [he proceeds].
When the sacrificial porridge has been slightly cooked, one should brandish a flaming torch clockwise around the clarified butter and the porridge;
then,
taking the *sruva* ladle with the right hand, one should hold it facing eastward.
Having likewise heated it face-downward over the fire, holding it with the left hand, one should cleanse it from the base to the tip using the tips of the *darbha* blades held in the right hand;
and from the tip to the base using the bases of the blades, starting from the tip and proceeding downward.
Then, having wiped [the vessel] down to its base with the consecrated water (praṇīta), he should sprinkle it again as before and heat it over the right side.
Then, having lifted up the clarified butter (ājya) from the east of the sacrificial pot (caru), he should place it [in the vessel]. ||48-49||
Having led [the vessel] to the north of the fire and placed the *caru* there, he should then lift it up,
lead it behind the clarified butter (*ājya*), and then lead it to the north of the *ājya*. Having placed the *ājya* behind the fire, he should indeed bring the *caru* forward.
Having brought [the clarified butter] and placed it to the north of the *ājya*, one should then proceed as before.
Then, having purified the *ājya* with the two strainers (*pavitra*) and inspected it,
one should remove any impurities and perform the purification of the *prokṣiṇī* water once more.
Then, taking the sacrificial grass from the *upayama* with his right hand and placing it in his left,
the sacrificer should rise while meditating on Prajāpati in his heart;
he should silently cast three fuel sticks smeared with clarified butter into the fire.
Having sat down, and having sprinkled the fire with water from the *prokṣaṇī* vessel using the *pavitra* strainers,
held in the right palm,
he should then perform the circumambulatory sprinkling (*pariṣecana*) starting from the northeast and ending in the north.
Then, with the right knee lowered and grasped by the Brahman priest with the tip of a *kuśa* blade,
and likewise grasped by the sacrificer,
the performer of the sacrifice should offer oblations of clarified butter with the *sruva* ladle into the kindled fire.

Beginning from the *ādhāra* oblation and continuing through the twelve *āhuti*s, the residue of each respective offering—the ghee clinging to the *sruva* ladle—must be poured into the *prokṣaṇī* vessel; such is the procedure. (57–58)
If one desires [to perform] a fire-oblation (homa), it should be performed there as appropriate:
"Oṃ, svāhā to Prajāpati; this is for Prajāpati, [my] salutation. "Oṃ, svāhā to Indra; this is for Indra, [my] salutation to the two Āghāra-offerings."

Om, svāhā to Agni; this [offering] is for Agni. Om, obeisance to me. || 2.152.60 || Om, svāhā to Soma; this [offering] is for Soma; obeisance to me regarding the two portions of clarified butter (ājyabhāgau).
Om bhūḥ, svāhā; this [offering] is for bhūḥ. Obeisance to me. Bhuvaḥ, svāhā; this [offering] is for bhuvaḥ. || 61 ||
Oṃ svaḥ svāhā—this is Svaḥ; these are the Great Utterances (Mahāvyāhṛtis).
Oṃ "tvanno agne"—this is for Agni and Varuṇa, and obeisance, Oṃ.
Oṃ "satvano agne"—this is for Agni and Varuṇa, and obeisance, Oṃ.
"Oṃ mayāśca agne" and "idaṃ agnaye namaḥ"—this is for Agni;
Oṃ. "Oṃ ye te śatam" with "svāhā"—this is for Savitṛ and Viṣṇu;
and this is for the Viśvedevas, the Maruts, and the Arkas—Oṃ, this. (64)
Oṃ *ud uttamaṃ* and so forth, svāhā; this is for Varuṇa, obeisance.
Like armor, it is said to be the warding off of divine obstacles and a source of peace.
Oṃ, the waters are auspicious, most auspicious, and peaceful.
May those most peaceful ones grant healing medicine.
Thus should the Brahmins perform the sprinkling (prokṣaṇa) in all the fire-pits, completing the ritual up to the sprinkling of the fires. 66.

Then the preceptor, having worshipped the fire, should perform the oblation to the planets (*grahahoma*). The sacrificial fuel-sticks (*samidh*) are, in order: *arka*, *palāśa*, *khadira*, *apāmārga*, *pippala*, *audumbara*, *śamī*, *dūrvā*, and *kuśa*.

One should understand that for the nine planets, the sacrificial fuel-sticks (samidh) are smeared with curd, milk, and ghee. Reciting the mantras, one should indeed offer oblations— either one hundred and eight, or twenty-eight, or eight times over— accompanied by the Śākalya formulas.
Oṃ *ākṛṣṇena* iti vai svāhā; this is indeed for Sūrya. O *imaṃ deva* iti vai svāhā; this is indeed for Candramas. Oṃ *agniḥ* iti vai svāhā; this is indeed for Bhauma.
Oṃ *udbudhyasva* svāhā! This is indeed an offering to Budha.
Oṃ *bṛhaspate* svāhā! This is indeed an offering to Bṛhaspati. Oṃ *annāt* svāhā! This is indeed an offering to Śukra. 7.1–7.2.
Oṃ *śannaḥ* svāhā; this is indeed for Śanaiścara. Oṃ *kayā naḥ* svāhā; this is indeed for Rāhu. Oṃ *ketum* svāhā; this is indeed for Ketu. (73)
Then, holding water in his hand, he should pour it upon the ground with the words, "May the planetary deities be pleased by this oblation;
salutations. Thereafter, he should perform the oblation for the presiding deities of the nine planets.

Eight or four auspicious fuel-sticks (*samidh*) of *pālāśa* wood, measuring a span (*prādeśa*) in length and originating from trees such as the *īśvara*, should be offered individually along with clarified butter;
likewise, sesame seeds mixed with clarified butter and barley should be offered according to the prescribed ritual injunctions.
Oṃ, we worship Tryambaka; svāhā! This is for Īśvara; obeisance to him.
(77) Oṃ, Śrī and Lakṣmī are yours; svāhā! This is for Haimavatī; obeisance to her. Oṃ, when you first cried out; svāhā! This is for Skanda; obeisance to him. (78)
Oṃ, you are the wide realm of Viṣṇu; svāhā! This is for Viṣṇu; obeisance to him.
Oṃ, Brahmā is the first to know; svāhā! This is for Brahmā; obeisance to him. Oṃ, Indra is the protector; svāhā! This is for Indra; obeisance to him.
Oṃ, for Yama, for Makha, svāhā! This is for Yama; obeisance to him. (2.152.80) Oṃ, you are the plougher, svāhā! This is for Kāla; Oṃ, obeisance to him.
Oṃ, O Citrāvasu, svāhā! This is for Citragupta; obeisance to him. (81)
"May the presiding deities be pleased by this oblation of substances.
Having uttered "namas," the sacrificer should pour out water.
Then, after that, follows the oblation for the secondary deities in due order.
Oṃ *agnim dūtam* iti svāhā; this indeed is for Agni, obeisance.
Oṃ *apsv agne* iti svāhā; this is for the Waters, obeisance. Oṃ *syonā pṛthivī* iti svāhā; this is for the Earth, obeisance. 84.
Oṃ *viṣṇorarāṭam*—svāhā! This is for Viṣṇu; Oṃ, salutation to him. Oṃ *sajoṣāḥ*—svāhā! This is for Indra; Oṃ, salutation to him. Oṃ *ādityaiḥ*—svāhā! This is for Indrāṇī; Oṃ, salutation to her.
Oṃ *brahma yajñānam* iti svāhā; this [is] for Brahmā, Oṃ, salutation to me. (86) Oṃ *namo astu* iti svāhā; this [is] for the serpents, Oṃ, salutation to me.
Oṃ *prajāpate* iti svāhā; this [is] for Prajāpati, salutation to me. (87)
"May the presiding lords be pleased by this oblation of substances.
Having uttered "namas," the sacrificer should pour out water.
Then follows the oblation for the five world-protectors according to the prescribed rite.

Oṃ *gaṇānām* iti svāhā—this [offering] is for Gaṇeśa; Oṃ, it is mine. Oṃ *ambe ambālike* svāhā—this [offering] is for Ambikā; it is mine. Oṃ *vāto vāmana* svāhā—this [offering] is for Vāyu; Oṃ, it is mine. (2.152.90)
Oṃ *ghṛtam* *ghṛta* svāhā! This [offering] is for Ākāśa; Oṃ, salutation to me. Oṃ *yāvāṅkaśa* svāhā! This [offering] is for the Aśvins; Oṃ, salutation to me.
(91) By this oblation of substances, may the guardians of the world be pleased.
Having uttered "namama," the performer of the sacrifice should cast water [into the fire].
Then follows the oblation for the guardians of the ten directions according to the prescribed rule:
"Oṃ trātāram indraṃ svāhā; this is for Indra, namama. (92–93)
*Oṃ agnidūtam iti svāhā; this is for Agni, may it be mine.
Oṃ yamāya tvā iti svāhā; this is indeed for Yama, may it be mine.
Oṃ asunvanta iti svāhā; this is for Nirṛti, may it be mine.* (94)

Oṃ *varuṇasya* iti svāhā; this is for Varuṇa, salutation to him. (95) Oṃ *vāyo ye te* iti svāhā; and this is for Vāyu, salutation to him. Oṃ *kuvid aṅga* iti svāhā; this is for Kubera, salutation to him. (96)
Oṃ *tam īśānam* iti svāhā; this is for Īśāna, may it be mine.
Oṃ *asme rudrā* iti svāhā; this is for Brahmā, may it be mine.
Oṃ *syonā pṛthivī* iti svāhā; this is for Ananta, may it be mine.
"By this oblation of substances, may the guardians of the directions be pleased.
Having uttered "namas," the sacrificer should cast forth water.
[He should offer] perfume, flowers, water, food offerings, lamps, and incense.
"I offer betel-leaf; may the Supreme Lords be pleased.
O Rādhikā, one should perform the worship in this manner according to the prescribed rule. Thus spoke Anādi Śrī Kṛṣṇa Nārāyaṇa in accordance with the injunctions.
"And that which was spoken for one devoted to the temple of the gods has also been told by me to you.

(101) Thus ends the one hundred and fifty-second chapter, titled "The Description of the Worship of the Vessel and its Guardian Deities, the Invitation, the Prokṣaṇī Vessel and other items, the Caru, the Ghee Oblation, the Warding Off, the Planetary Homa, the Homa for the Adhidevas and Pratyadhidevas, the Homa for the World-Guardians and Directional Guardians," etc., in the second section, the Tretā-santāna, of the glorious *Lakṣmī-Nārāyaṇīya Saṃhitā*. (152)

Śrī Kṛṣṇa said:
O Rādhā, thereafter, one should perform the fire-offering (homa) for the deities residing in the site according to the prescribed rules;
I shall tell you that which Hari has declared for His devotee, as well as other rites. || 1 ||
In that regard, for those beginning with Śikhin and the others, one should first offer oblations ending with "svāhā" and preceded by the Praṇava (Oṃ),
using their names and Vedic mantras, one hundred and eight times for each;
or twenty-eight, or eight, oblations of sesame, clarified butter, and milk-rice.
And fuel-sticks should be offered, specifically those made of *udumbara* wood.
(3) In its absence, other fuel-sticks of *aśvattha* wood, combined with honey, clarified butter, and milk, should be offered;
likewise, black sesame seeds should be offered according to the prescribed rite and preceded by mantras. (4)
Oṃ, svāhā to Śikhin; this is for Śikhin, [I offer] salutation.
Oṃ, svāhā to Parjanya; this is for Parjanya. Oṃ, svāhā to Jayanta; this is for Jayanta.
Om, to Indra indeed, Svāhā! This is for Indra; obeisance. (6) Om, to Sūrya indeed, Svāhā! This is for Sūrya; obeisance. Om, to Satya indeed, Svāhā! Here is for Satya; obeisance. (7)
Oṃ, svāhā to Bhṛśa; this is for Bhṛśa, salutation to him. Oṃ, svāhā to Ākāśa; this is for Ākāśa. (8) Oṃ, svāhā to Vāyu; this is for Vāyu, salutation to him.
Oṃ, obeisance to Pūṣan, svāhā! This is for Pūṣan, obeisance.
Oṃ, svāhā to Vitatha! This is for Vitatha, obeisance. Oṃ, svāhā to Gṛhakṣata! This is for Gṛhakṣata. (2.153.10)
Oṃ, svāhā to Yama; this is for Yama, salutation. Oṃ, svāhā to the Gandharva; this is for the Gandharva, salutation.
Oṃ, svāhā to Bhṛṅgarāja; this is for Bhṛṅga, salutation.
Oṃ, svāhā to Mṛga; this is for Mṛga, salutation to him.
Oṃ, svadhā to the Pitṛs; this is for the Pitṛs, salutation to them. Oṃ, svāhā to Dauvārika; this is for Dauvārika. || 12-13 ||
Oṃ, svāhā to Sugrīva; this is for Sugrīva. Oṃ, svāhā to Puṣpadanta; this is for Puṣpa, [my] salutation. Oṃ, svāhā to Varuṇa; this is for Varuṇa, [my] salutation.
Oṃ, svāhā to Asura; this is for Asura, salutation to him.
Oṃ, svāhā indeed to Śeṣa; this is for Śeṣa, salutation to him. Oṃ, svāhā to Pāpayakṣman; this is for Pāpayakṣman, salutation to him. 15–16.
Oṃ, svāhā to Disease! This is for Disease; salutation to Disease. Oṃ, svāhā to the Serpent! This is for the Serpent; salutation to the Serpent.
Oṃ, svāhā to Mukhya! This is for Mukhya; salutation to Mukhya. 17.
Oṃ, svāhā to Bhallāṭa; this is for Bhallāṭaka.
Oṃ, svāhā indeed to Soma; this is mine, dedicated to Soma. Oṃ, svāhā indeed to the Serpent; this is mine, dedicated to the Serpent. 18–19.
Om, svāhā to Aditi; this is for Aditi, my salutation. Om, svāhā indeed to Diti; this is for Diti, my salutation.
Om, likewise svāhā to the Adityas; this is for the Adityas, my salutation. 2.153.20. Om, svāhā to the Adityas; this is for the Adityas, my salutation.
Oṃ, svāhā to Sāvitra; this is for Sāvitra, [I offer] salutation.
Oṃ, svāhā indeed to Jaya; this is for Jaya, [I offer] salutation.
Oṃ, svāhā indeed to Rudra; this is for Rudra, [I offer] salutation. 21–22.
Oṃ, indeed, svadhā to Aryaman; this is for Aryaman, obeisance. Oṃ, indeed, svāhā to Savitṛ; this is for Savitṛ, obeisance.
Oṃ, svāhā to Vivasvat; this is for Vivasvat, obeisance. 23.
Oṃ, svāhā to Vibudheśa; this is for Vibudheśa, salutation to him. Oṃ, svāhā to Mitra; this is for Mitra, salutation to him.
Oṃ, svāhā to Rājayakṣman; this is for Rājayakṣman, salutation to him. 24–25.
Oṃ pṛthvīdhṛke svāhā; this is for Pṛthvīdhṛk, [I offer] salutation. Oṃ āpavatsāya svāhā; this is for Āpavatsa, [I offer] salutation.
Oṃ brahmaṇe ca vai svāhā; this is for Brahmā, [I offer] salutation.
Oṃ, svāhā to Carakī! This is for Carakī; salutation to her. (27) Oṃ, svāhā to Vidārī! This is for Vidārī; salutation to her.
Oṃ, svāhā to Pūtanā! This is for Pūtanā; salutation to her. (28)
Oṃ, svāhā to the evil rākṣasī; this is for the evil rākṣasī, not for me.
Oṃ, svāhā to Skanda; this is for Skanda, not for me. Svadhā indeed to Aryaman; this is for Aryaman, not for me.
Oṃ jṛmbhakāya ca svāhā; this is for Jṛmbha, [I offer] salutation. Oṃ pilipicchāya svāhā; this is for Pilipiccha, [I offer] salutation.
Om indrāya ca vai svāhā; this is for Indra, [I offer] salutation. 2.153.30–31.
Oṃ, svāhā to Agni; this is for Agni, my salutation. Oṃ, svāhā to Yama; this is for Yama, my salutation.
Oṃ, svāhā to Nirṛti; this is for Nirṛti, my salutation. 32.
Oṃ, svāhā to Varuṇa; this is for Varuṇa, [I offer] salutation.
Oṃ, svāhā indeed to Vāyu; this is for Vāyu, [I offer] salutation.
Oṃ, svāhā to Kubera; this is indeed for Kubera, [I offer] salutation. 34.
Om, svāhā to Īśāna; this indeed is for Īśāna, salutation to him.
Om, svāhā to Brahmā; this indeed is for Brahmā, salutation to him.
Om, svāhā to Ananta; this indeed is for Ananta, salutation to him. (35)
Oṃ, svāhā to Ugrasena; this is for Ugrasena, salutation to him.
Oṃ, svāhā to Ḍāmara; this is for Ḍāmara, salutation to him. Oṃ, vaṣaṭ to Mahākāla; this is for Mahākāla, salutation to him. 36–37.
Om, Svāhā to the two Aśvins; this is for the two Aśvins.
Om, Svāhā to Durgā; this is for Durgā.
(38) By this oblation, may Śikhin and the others be pleased; one should then cast water [into the fire].
Then, for Vāstoṣpati, one should likewise offer one hundred and eight oblations consisting of fuel-sticks,
sesame seeds, milk-rice, and clarified butter, joined with mantras; indeed,
those [oblations] are twenty-seven for each individual mantra.
Oṃ, O Lord of the Dwelling (Vāstoṣpati), acknowledge us! Be one who grants us easy access and be free from disease for us.
Whatever we implore you for, favor that with your approval. Be auspicious to our bipeds and auspicious to our quadrupeds; Svāhā! Svāhā to this Vāstoṣpati; obeisance to Vāstoṣpati.
I offer incense, a lamp, food offerings, and water.
Oṃ Vāstoṣpati, be our protector;
O Indu, increase our wealth with cattle and horses.
May we be unaging in your friendship; like a father toward his sons, be gracious to us.
Be a source of well-being for our bipeds and a blessing for our quadrupeds. Svāhā!
Svāhā to Vāstoṣpati! Adoration to Vāstoṣpati!
I offer incense, a lamp, food offerings, and water.
Oṃ Vāstoṣpate, may we ever abide in your auspicious and golden dwelling that grants us prosperity.
Protect us in peace and in exertion; O Lord, grant us boons.
Do you all protect us always with blessings. Svāhā!
Svāhā to Vāstoṣpati! Adoration to Vāstoṣpati!
I offer incense, a lamp, food offerings, and water.
Oṃ, O Lord of the Dwelling, who removes affliction, entering into all forms, be our most gracious friend; svāhā! May you increase us with prosperity.
"Vāstoṣpataye svāhā! Vāstoṣpataye namaḥ!
I offer incense, a lamp, food offerings, and water.
Then, indeed, six oblations are made with the *sthālīpāka* as follows:
Om, I invoke Agni, Indra, Bṛhaspati, and all the gods;
and Sarasvatī and Vājina—grant me a dwelling-place, O Vājinas! Svāhā!
This [is for] Agni, Indra, Bṛhaspati, the Viśvedevas, Sarasvatī, and Vājina. 2.153.50.

Oṃ! To all the serpents and divine beings, to Himavat and Sudarśana, to the Vasus, the Rudras, the Ādityas, and Īśāna together with the world-protectors—to all these I go for refuge. Grant me the dwelling-place, O Vājins! Svāhā!
This [is offered] with Svāhā and obeisance to the serpents, the divine folk, to Himavat, to Sudarśana, to the Vasus, the Rudras, the Ādityas, to Īśāna, and to the Jagadīs; Om,
to both the forenoon and the afternoon, together with midday.
The evening, midnight, the goddess Dawn, and the great path—to all these I resort.
Grant me a dwelling for my horse; svāhā!
Homage to this [deity] for the forenoon, the afternoon, the evening, the midnight, the dawn, the goddess, and the great path.
Om! Homage to the creator, the transformer, Viśvakarman, the plants, and the lords of the forest.
I take refuge in all these; may the swift ones grant me a dwelling, svāhā!
(55) Homage to this maker, the fashioner, Viśvakarman, to the plants, and to the trees!
Oṃ, together with Dhātṛ, Vidhātṛ, and the Lord of the treasures... (56)
I take refuge in all these; may the horses grant me a dwelling, svāhā!
This [offering] is for Dhātṛ, Vidhātṛ, and the Lord of Treasures; obeisance to them. Om! May this dwelling be pleasant and auspicious; it is granted by Brahmā, Prajāpati, and all the deities, svāhā!
"Salutation to Brahmā, to Prajāpati, and to all the deities.

(58) Again, he should offer a bilva fruit together with clarified butter and seeds, either with the mantra "O Lord of the Dwelling" (*vāstoṣpate*) alone or along with the mantras that are about to be mentioned. (59)
Holding the fifth offering, a bilva fruit mixed with clarified butter, and reciting the mantra, one should indeed perform one hundred and eight oblations for each, according to the prescribed rule:
"Oṃ Vāstoṣpati! You are the firm pillar; you have come to this sacrificial session. You are the drop that shatters the eternal fortresses."
May Indra, the friend of the sages, be auspicious to us—both to our bipeds and to our quadrupeds. Svāhā! This [is for] Vāstoṣpati.
To those who are not terrible, and to those who are terrible, and to those more terrible than the most terrible;
to all of them, to all the forms of Śarva—to you who possess the forms of Rudra, let there be obeisance.
One should perform more than a hundred oblations for the purpose of joining the vital points (*marmans*) of the site (*vāstu*).
Having offered again to Śikhin and the others, and having worshipped them with the fivefold offerings (*pañcopacāra*),
one should likewise [worship] the image of Vāstu situated upon the pedestal with curd, a ladle (*darvī*), and so forth.

Having placed uncooked clay vessels filled with *śaivala*, the seven types of grain, perfumes, unbroken rice, flowers, and so forth, and having covered them, one should deposit them either in the southeast corner of the temple or in the northern corner from that [southeast] point. (64–65)
Having filled the hollow at the knee with water in the space designated for the sky,
one should scatter fragrant flowers there and place an earthen vessel;
while reciting "Obeisance to Varuṇa," one should fill that clay vessel with earth.
Having thus made the oblation to the deities of the site (vāstudeva), one should then offer it to the Yoginīs:
"Oṃ divyayoginyai svāhā; this [is] for the divine Yoginī, obeisance to her. In the same way, everything should be applied, including "obeisance to the Yoginī."
Oṃ, to Mahāśabdā, Siddhi, Gaṇeśvarī, svāhā! To Namama.
To Pretākṣī, Ḍākinī, Kāmī, Kālarātri, svāhā! To Namama.
To Niśācarī, Huṃkārī, Siddhivaitālī, svāhā! To Namama.
Hrīṃ! To the one whose purpose is the syllable *hrīṃ*, to Bhūtaḍāmā, to the one with upraised hair—*svāhā*, obeisance to her.
(2.153.70) To the one with deformed eyes, to the one with emaciated limbs, to the devourer of men—*svāhā*, obeisance to her.
To the one who performs the *phuṭ*-sound, to Vīrabhadra, and to the smoke-eyed one—*svāhā*, obeisance to her. (71)
To Kālapriyā, the Rākṣasī, the terrible Rākṣasī, svāhā!
To Virūpākṣī, the terrifying one, the large-eyed one, svāhā!
To Kaumārī, Caṇḍikā, Vārāhī, and Muṇḍamātā, svāhā! Homage to them! 72.
To Bhairavī, Cakriṇī, Krodhā, and Durmukhī, Svāhā! Adoration! To Pretavāhā, Kuraṅgī, and Pralambauṣṭhī, Svāhā! Adoration!
To Mālinī, Mantrayoginī, and Kālaghnī, Svāhā! Adoration!
To Mohinī, to Vakrā, to Kuṇḍalinī, to Bālakī—svāhā! Adoration!
To Kaumārī, to Yamadūtī, to Karālī, to Kauśikī—svāhā! Adoration!
To Yakṣiṇī, to Bhakṣiṇī, to Kumārikā—svāhā! Adoration!
To Yantravādinī, Viśālākṣī, Kāmukī—svāhā! Adoration to me!
To Vyāghrī, Rākṣasī, Pretabhakṣiṇī—svāhā! Adoration to me!
To Dhūrjaṭī, Vikaṭā, Ghorā, Kapālī—svāhā! Adoration to me!
"To Vikalā, Mālā, and Sarvasiddhi, svāhā! Homage to me!
May the sixty-four Yoginīs indeed be pleased by this oblation.
The performer of the sacrifice should perform the fire-oblation for the Kṣetrapāla according to the prescribed rule."
Oṃ, svāhā to the Ageless One; this is indeed my salutation to the Ageless One.
Svāhā to Pāvaka, to Caura, to Dakṣa, and to him whose form is Indra;
svāhā to Kuṣmāṇḍa, to Varuṇa, and to Bāhuka; [this] salutation is mine. 2.153.80.
To Nimukta, to Liptaka, to Tilalopa, svāhā! Adoration! To Ekadaṃṣṭra, to Airāvata, to Auṣadhighna, svāhā! Adoration!
To Bandhana, to Ādivyāpta, to Kambala, svāhā! Adoration!
To the Lord who agitates, to the one who supports the earth, svāhā! Adoration!
To the subtle one, to the restrainer of the moon, to the one with a raised neck, svāhā! Adoration!
To the one with a broad chest, to the matted-haired one, to the Season, svāhā! Adoration! 82–83.
To Maheśvara, to Vikāra, to Maṇimā—svāhā! Adoration!
To Guṇabandha, to Ḍāmara, to Dṛḍhakiraṇa—svāhā! Adoration!
To Sthavila, to Dantura, to Dhanada—svāhā! Adoration!
To the one who makes the nāgas and produces foam, svāhā! Adoration!
To the one with great feet, the long-bodied lion, svāhā! Adoration!
To the deer, the bird, and the one whose vehicle is a lion, svāhā! Adoration! 85–86.
Svāhā! Adoration to Tīkṣṇauṣṭha, Alābha, and Sruktuṇḍa!

Then, with the mantra "mūrdhānaṃ divaḥ," they should offer the final oblation (pūrṇāhuti);
at that time, the falling of the oblations is considered to take place in the peace-pot (śāntighaṭa).
O Rādhā, such was what Hari said regarding the construction of a temple for the deity.
"I have told you all this procedure, which yields fruit through mere hearing.

Thus ends the one hundred and fifty-seventh chapter, titled "Description of the Installation, Worship, Offering of Balis, Homa, and Other Rites Pertaining to the Form [of the Deity]— including the Months, Seasons, Yugas, Colors, Vedas, Vasus, Guardians of the Quarters, World-Guardians, Kṣetrapālas, Incarnations of the Lord, Sacrificial Weapons, Ornaments, Beloved Principles, Root Mantras, the Two Gāyatrīs, the Arpaṇa Mantra, the Puruṣasūkta, and Nyāsa"— in the second section, the Tretā-Saṃtāna, of the *Śrī Lakṣmī-Nārāyaṇīya Saṃhitā*.
